LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup, plus a preview and prediction Patrick Smith/Getty Images In the Week 10 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the New York Giants play host to the division rival Washington Commanders . New York enters this game riding high atop the NFC East, having won each of its last two games sandwiching a Week 8 bye. The Giants are surprisingly in the playoff picture in the first year of the John Harbaugh era despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2. They recently turned to J.J. McCarthy in place of Jameis Winston but kept on winning. Washington climbed out of last place in the NFC East thanks to a Week 8 win over the lowly Philadelphia Eagles but still has the second-worst record in the conference. The Commanders missed an opportunity for a win the last time these two teams played by mismanaging the clock as poorly as any team ever has, and they will surely be looking to atone for that mistake here. Will the Giants keep rolling, or will the Commanders capture a rare victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Giants vs. Commanders live Date: Thursday, Nov. 12 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, New Jersey) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Giants -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball The Commanders are not particularly effective either passing or running the football. They rank 21st in the NFL in net yards per pass attempt (which accounts for yards lost to sacks), and they're 23rd in designed rushing yards per carry, which eliminates scrambling from the picture. Their most effective form of offense is scrambling, where Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have run 29 times for 274 yards — the most scramble yards in the NFL, per Tru Media. But that's not something that you can lean on down-to-down. Daniels has completed only 63.9% of his passes at an average of 6.9 yards per attempt. While he has seven passing touchdowns and has yet to be intercepted, he has a low passing success rate (43.9%, according to Tru Media), has generated explosives at only an average rate (7.8%) and has struggled on third downs (30.9%). Again, his most effective way of moving the ball has been via the scramble. The Giants are actually second in the NFL in passing success rate allowed and third in explosives per dropback, according to Tru Media. So Daniels, with his limited receiving corps in the absence of Terry McLaurin , might find it difficult to move the ball through the air. The Giants, though, have been vulnerable to opponent scrambles, allowing quarterbacks to take off downfield on a league-high 23.9% of pressured dropbacks and yielding 225 scramble yards to date. So Daniels could have some room to run. In the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt , the Commies have turned to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the backfield. They have not been particularly effective on the ground, but they're each capable outlet receivers for Daniels, who has targeted backs on 14.4% of his passes, a slightly higher rate than last year (12.8%). Doing so against the Giants may not be the most advisable strategy, though, because it means testing rookie linebacker Arvell Reese in space, and Reese has been a space-eating demon so far this season. Daniels' other pass-catchers at the moment are Stefon Diggs , Antonio Williams , Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo. The Giants have been good at limiting tight ends over the middle (there's Reese showing up again), so the passing game might run through the perimeter receivers, who will face off with an improved Deonte Banks and the recently-extended Greg Newsome II on the outside. Look for Daniels to at least try to test those guys deep down the field, given he has the seventh-highest deep throw rate among qualified quarterbacks. The Giants have faced deep passes at essentially an average rate so far this season, and they've been excellent at defending them, checking in second in EPA per dropback on those plays. Still, dinking and dunking hasn't been all that effective for Daniels and the Commanders, so they're going to have to try to hit on a few big plays. When the Giants have the ball The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy as their quarterback in garbage time of their loss to the Saints back in Week 6, and they have stuck with him over the last two games. They've been a somewhat unusual offense with McCarthy under center. McCarthy himself has not been efficient on a down-to-down basis. He's completed only 63.2% of his passes, and he has one touchdown pass and one interception. He checks in 31st in success rate among 37 quarterbacks with at least 75 dropbacks this season, according to Tru Media. But McCarthy is averaging 9.1 (!!!!) yards per attempt, and he's 15th among the same group of 37 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's because when he does complete passes, they're basically all going for big gains in big situations. He's throwing the ball farther downfield than anyone in the league (10.6-yard average depth of target), and he's leading the NFL in explosive plays per dropback at 16.0%, per Tru Media. The Commanders' defense is essentially the opposite of what McCarthy has done so far. They yield a high passing success rate (21st in the league) but a low explosive rate (11th). The tension between those two poles will be interesting to watch play out on Monday night. When McCarthy drops back to pass, he is looking most often to Malik Nabers , who has been the intended receiver on 31.7% of McCarthy's throws. Malachi Fields , not Isaiah Likely , has been the secondary target, with a 20.6% target share compared to Likely's 17.5% rate. Before McCarthy took over at quarterback, Likely tied Nabers for the team lead in target share at 29.4%, compared to just 11.2% for Fields. Nabers and Fields will do most of their work against Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson on the outside, while Likely will see a lot of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles , slot corner Mike Sainristil and safeties Jeremy Reaves and Nick Cross . The Commanders have not generated very much pressure this season (33.5% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media, 25th in the league), while McCarthy has been one of the league's most-pressured quarterbacks since taking over. He tends to hold the ball for a while as he looks to push it down the field. Whether the Commanders can get after him will go a long way toward determining whether he can complete any big plays. Cam Skattebo is back for the Giants in this game, and he's likely to take over the lead role from Devin Singletary , who struggled last week and is more suited to being a passing-down back. Skattebo hasn't been very effective as a rusher this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry with a 45.9% success rate, but he had his best game of the year before sitting out last week after the bye. The Commanders have been solid against the run, yielding only 3.9 yards per carry, with below-average marks both before (1.09) and after contact (2.83). This might be a game where the Giants lean on those big plays from McCarthy. I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. New York (5-2-1) is in first place in the division and in a prime spot to make the playoffs even with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart sidelined with a knee injury. Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy have done enough filling in for the injured quarterback, and the Giants find themselves as favorites on Thursday with McCarthy set to start. These two teams played one of the wilder games of the 2026 season back in Week 5, as they tied 27-27. Washington (now 2-5-1 this season) had a major blunder at the end of the game, running out the clock before getting a chance to take a game-winning field goal. That came right after a brutal fumble by Giants running back Cam Skattebo with the team driving for a potential field goal to win the game. Since these teams tied, the winner of Thursday’s matchup will have the head-to-head tiebreaker, which could be extremely valuable in the playoff race. All week long, the SI Betting team has been making game picks, player prop selections and more for this NFC East clash. I’ve narrowed things down to four of our favorite plays to give bettors a one-stop shop for Commanders vs. Giants to open the second half of the 2026 NFL regular season. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Commanders vs. Giants Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook New York Giants -1.5 (-110) vs. Washington Commanders – Iain MacMillan Malik Nabers OVER 5.5 Receptions (-138) – Peter Dewey Jayden Daniels OVER 35.5 Rushing Yards (-110) – Peter Dewey Isaiah Likely Anytime TD (+190) – Peter Dewey Earlier this week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite pick for every game in Week 10 in his Road to 272 column . He’s targeting New York as a home favorite to cover: I may have included the New York Giants in last week's edition of my Fraud Rankings , but my biggest issue with them has been their strength of schedule. Will I be betting on them when they take on teams like the Jaguars and 49ers in the coming weeks? Likely not, but they once again have a game against a bad team on Thursday Night Football when they face the Washington Commanders, and much like the majority of the season, I expect them to take care of business against an inferior opponent. These two teams played to a tie in Week 5 earlier this season, but with it being a road game for the Giants and the fact that they had Jameis Winston at quarterback, I think we can admit they're in a better spot in the rematch. J.J. McCarthy has been surprisingly solid to begin his tenure with the Giants, ranking fifth in the NFL in completion percentage over expected (+5.3%) amongst quarterbacks who have played 60+ snaps this season. It's also no coincidence that over the last three weeks, the Giants have led the league in net yards per play at +1.5. Meanwhile, the Commanders continue to be a poorly coached team that doesn't thrive in any area, ranking in the bottom half of the NFL in virtually every metric. The Giants have played three quarterbacks this season – Dart, Winston and now McCarthy – yet Nabers has remained productive no matter what. The former first-round pick has 78 targets in eight games, reeling in 53 passes for 648 yards and two scores. While he hasn’t found the end zone a bunch in 2026, Nabers has at least six grabs in five of his eight games and has four straight matchups with at least eight targets. He had a huge game against Washington earlier this season, pulling down 11 of his 20 targets for 121 yards and a score. The Commanders have struggled against the pass all season long, ranking 18th in the league in passing yards allowed while also allowing the sixth-most passing scores. I expect Nabers to be heavily involved in the game plan once again on Thursday night. Daniels torched the Giants on the ground in Week 5, rushing nine times for 103 yards and two scores. He has just two games this season with over 35.5 rushing yards, but Daniels has really killed the Giants on the ground in his NFL career. The star quarterback has 44, 35, 68 and 103 rushing yards in his four games against the division rival, and New York has given up the third-most rushing yards to the quarterback position in 2026. A lot of that is because of Daniels’ big game, but I like this matchup for the Commanders signal-caller on Thursday. New York has struggled to get home this season, posting the worst pressure rate in the NFL while picking up just 16 sacks in eight games. Even though the Giants are third in the NFL in success rate, they have shown that they can’t keep contain on Daniels, who is one of the best athletes in open space in the league. Giants tight end Isaiah Likely has been a touchdown machine in the 2026 season, reeling in 46 of his 69 targets for 448 yards and six scores. He’s coming off a score in Week 9 against Philly, and Likely has a couple of multi-score games in 2026. Plus, he’s been a beast when the Giants get near the end zone. In the red zone, Likely has nine targets in 2026, turning those into eight catches and five touchdowns. He hasn’t missed a beat with the New York quarterback changes, finding the end zone in Weeks 1, 5, 6 and 9. Yes, he scored against Washington in the overtime matchup in Week 5, catching 11 of his 13 targets for 94 yards and two scores. The Commanders have allowed eight touchdown passes to opposing tight ends in 2026 – the second-most in the NFL. At nearly 2/1, Likely is a great bet to lead this Giants offense once again in Week 10. away.headline: Washington Commanders QB named as new star of 'The Bachelor'
away.blurb: Mail Search the web Search with Yahoo Scout Advertisement Advertisement Return to Homepage Entertainment: Maybe Palmer can coach Hartman on what life as The Bachelor is like. Hopefully for the Commanders quarterback, he's more successful than Palmer was on the show. After choosing law student Jessica Bowlin, the relationship quickly flamed out. Naturally, that's not all that surprising. Through 2024, only 11 of 49 couples who featured on The Bachelor or The Bachelorette remained together. Washington Commanders QB named as new star of 'The Bachelor' Search Query for Search the web Search with Yahoo Scout Search the web Skip to main New movies to watch this weekend Jim Caviezel’s action-film routine at 58 Kate Middleton on cancer recovery Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Former Notre Dame and Wake Forest quarterback Sam Hartman is currently a member of the Washington Commanders practice squad. But he's going to become a whole lot more famous and it has nothing to do with football. As the man with the best hair and beard combo in football, he's going to take those gifts to a place where they truly belong — The Bachelor . ABC announced that the 27-year-old Commanders quarterback will star in the upcoming season of the longtime matchmaking show when it debuts on March 21. Of course, Sam Hartman is not the first active NFL quarterback to appear on the program. All the way back in 2004, Jesse Palmer was the centerpiece of the show while he was a backup quarterback with the New York Giants. That caused a few issues with his NFL employer. General Manager Ernie Accorsi famously said about his escapades, "I would have been much happier if he was studying tape the last six weeks instead of getting involved with this thing." Palmer was eventually cut before the 2005 season and never suited up in the NFL again. However, he did embark on a long and successful media career . And to bring it all full circle, the ESPN analyst now serves as the host of The Bachelor . Will Hartman be able to balance the rigors of an NFL practice squad while looking for love in front of a nationally televised audience? The former Fighting Irish star has yet to appear in an NFL game since signing with the Commanders after going undrafted in 2024, bouncing on and off the practice squad. Maybe Sam Hartman can buck that trend next year and find true love. Maybe he can get promoted from the Commanders practice squad and make it in the NFL. Or if all else fails, he can always host Season 50 of The Bachelor in 2047. The post Washington Commanders QB Sam Hartman is ABC's next 'Bachelor' appeared first on Awful Announcing . home.headline: Washington Commanders Rule Out 2 Players Ahead of Thursday’s Giants Game
home.blurb: Washington Commanders Rule Out 2 Players Ahead of Thursday's Giants Game Washington has ruled out two players. Starting center Lucas Patrick will miss the game with a concussion, while tight end Colson Yankoff will sit out with a knee injury. As for wide receiver Treylon Burks , whose status remained uncertain because of a foot injury that kept him out last week, he no longer carries an injury designation and will return to the Commanders' offense. Outside linebacker Malik Harrison is the only player still carrying an injury designation. He's questionable with a groin injury, and the Giants will likely determine his availability closer to kickoff. Unlock the latest Heavy on Commanders news — direct to your inbox. The Washington Commanders are gearing up for arguably their biggest game of the season so far on Thursday night. They will travel to MetLife Stadium to take on the NFC East-leading Giants in a primetime matchup. The Commanders enter the game with a 2-5-1 record, while the Giants sit on the opposite end of the spectrum at 5-2-1. Both teams have a tie on their records after playing one another in a wild overtime finish a few weeks ago. Now, they meet for the final time this season, and if the Commanders want any chance of closing the gap in the division, this could very well be a must-win game. Both teams released their final injury reports on Wednesday. Although Washington has already dealt with a handful of season-ending injuries, the team has a fairly clean outlook heading into Thursday night. Neither player practiced at all this week, so these absences haven't caught Washington off guard. Nick Allegretti is expected to take over for Patrick at center. The final injury report for the New York Giants and the Washington Commanders ahead of their game at the Meadowlands on Thursday night. https://t.co/NO0AgGzk54 — Ralph Vacchiano (@RalphVacchiano) November 11, 2026 New York also has a relatively clean injury report heading into the prime-time showdown. Running back Cam Skattebo and quarterback J.J. McCarthy are both good to go after the Giants monitored their statuses throughout the week. New York Giants quarterback JJ McCarthy exited the team's Week 9 win over the Philadelphia Eagles after taking a massive hit from linebacker Zack Baun. He eventually returned to the game after a trip to the locker room, but the team has since revealed if it could affect his playing status moving forward. According to NFL insider Adam Schefter of ESPN , McCarthy suffered a hip pointer and the team is confident that he will be ready for Thursday night’s game against the Washington Commanders. That is certainly good news, given how the injury initially looked. He was in visible pain on the sideline before heading to the locker room and being replaced by backup quarterback Jameis Winston. The Giants traded a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for McCarthy following starter Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury in September. New York then switched to McCarthy as its starter ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the Houston Texans, and he has played quite well since, throwing for 622 yards, one touchdown and one interception.

Center Lucas Patrick and tight end Colson Yankoff have been ruled out for the game , and it'll be next man up for the Commanders. Patrick was placed in the concussion protocol during their game last week against the Los Angeles Rams. As for Yankoff, he's dealing with a knee injury. The Patriots, which are off to a 5-4 start, are coming off a 45-27 defeat at the hands of Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers. Meanwhile, the Lions, which are sitting at 6-2, defeated the Miami Dolphins, 19-9, in their Week 9 tilt . New England – led by Mike Vrabel on the sidelines – has lost two of its last three games, including to the Chicago Bears in Week 7. Additionally, it sits basically in the middle of the pack in both points scored (23.4/game) and points allowed (23.0/g). Yet, the Patriots still possess a myriad of talent on both sides of the ball. On offense, they're led under center by third-year passer Drake Maye, who has thrown for 18 touchdowns, 2,282 yards and a league-high 11 interceptions through nine games. He's coming off a three-interception performance against the Packers in which he completed a season-low 55.3 percent of his passes. Maye's top target this year has been veteran tight end Hunter Henry, who has amassed 32 catches, 361 yards and two touchdowns through the season's first nine games. And on the ground, the Patriots are spearheaded by sixth-year back Rhamondre Stevenson. Stevenson, a fourth-round pick of New England, has accumulated 399 yards and two touchdowns, and is presently averaging 3.9 yards per carry. Then, on the defensive side of the ball, the Patriots have received strong performances this season from the likes of EDGE defenders Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder, cornerback Carlton Davis III and linebacker Christian Elliss. Ponder, a second-year pro , has already recorded 7.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss and 13 QB hits, and has returned a fumble for a touchdown. And for his efforts, he's earned a 75.0 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, the 23rd-best overall grade among 110 qualified players at the position. The Patriots will not, however, have the services of Davis (knee) for this Week 10 international affair. Plus, they will also be down starting left guard Ben Brown (knee), and are expected to be without Stevenson (knee). Stevenson, the team's No. 1 back, suffered a plantaris tendon tear last week against the Packers. Those are three significant losses for Vrabel's squad going into its matchup with Detroit. As for the Lions, they will also be down multiple starters in Week 10: linebacker Jack Campbell (neck), center Cade Mays (ankle) and cornerback D.J. Reed (hip). Plus, safety Kerby Joseph, who has yet to play a single game in 2026, will not be making his season debut in Germany. While both teams are rather significantly banged up, I still believe this matchup favors Detroit. At this present juncture, I believe the Lions have a 59 percent chance to secure their fifth straight victory. The Detroit Lions (6-2) are headed to Munich, Germany, to take on the New England Patriots (5-4) in an overseas edition of Week 10 NFL Football. It's been 11 seasons since the Lions last played an international game, but this trip has been in the works for some time. In 2024, as part of the NFL's Global Markets Program, the Lions have had marketing rights in the DACH region , which includes Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Since then, the team has made several trips to Germany and has helped support Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown— whose mother, Miriam Brown, was born and raised in Germany —in running youth football programs across the country. As for the game itself, it looks like it'll be a good one, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -2.5 points . While the Lions are riding a four-game winning streak, the Patriots' 2026 season has been a more up-and-down affair after reaching the Super Bowl in 2025. They opened the season by losing to the Seahawks, beat the Steelers, then lost to the Jaguars over the first three weeks. They got back to 2-2 with a big win over the Bills, then rallied to 4-2 after wins over the Raiders and Jets. The Bears took them down on Thursday night in Week 7, but the Patriots eeked out a five-point win over the Dolphins to reach 5-3. On Sunday, the Patriots took on the Packers and looked completely unprepared. Packer QB Jordan Love jumped all over them, throwing for 372 yards and three scores, while Patriots Drake Maye threw for 299 yards and three scores, but also threw three interceptions and was sacked four times. On the ground, the Packers' worst-ranked rushing offense ran for 129 yards and two touchdowns, while the Pats gained 94 rushing yards, a touchdown, and lost a fumble. In the end, the Packers left Foxborough with a 45-27 win, and left former Patriots QB and current color commentator Tom Brady wondering who this New England team actually is: "Half the season they played like this, and the other half of the season they haven't turned the ball over, they haven't exposed the defense, have played more physical on defense, but right now it's just too inconsistent. Which team are they going to get? The team that is loose with the ball, is loose with decision-making, looking like they can be beaten by anybody. Or the team that takes care of the football, that makes the other team play left-handed, and can do what they want to do. Can they be a good team? They haven't quite done that because good teams leave the smallest margin of error." The Lions and Patriots are scheduled to play on Sunday, November 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Erik Schlitt · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions (6-2) and New England Patriots (5-4) will face off in a Week 10 interconference battle in Munich, Germany. "We understand the challenge here," Lions coach Dan Campbell said of the Patriots. "It's a very good team. It's a competitive team. They're going to clean up a lot of things, and we've got to be ready to go." This week's prediction preview is sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , who currently have the Lions listed at +1600 to win this year's Super Bowl and are currently 2.5-point favorites in Week 10 . Let's take a closer look at this matchup and predict how the Lions will earn a victory over the Patriots in this week's Honolulu Blueprint. Patriot s base scheme For a detailed look at the opposing scheme, check out our complementary breakdown piece: Lions Week 10 preview: Breaking down the Patriots' offensive and defensive schemes . Prediction 1: Gibbs attacks the EDGE in the run game The Lions and Patriots both have old-school coaches who are both direct or indirect descendants of the Bill Parcells coaching tree. And as you might expect, like Parcells, both coaches prioritize controlling the trenches by establishing the run on offense and stopping the run on defense. By the numbers, the Patriots' run defense looks strong. They're 10th in DVOA run defense, ninth in rush yards allowed per game (96.7) and per play (3.9), fifth in EPA per rush (-0.12), and third in yards before contact (0.57). Their success ties to a strong interior defensive line that can stuff the run in two- and three-down sets, featuring Milton Williams, Christian Barramore, and former Lion Corey Durden. It's tough to find room up the gut. Complicating things even further is how the Patriots deploy the blitz. Entering this game, the Patriots blitz 40.1% of the time (6th most in the NFL), and most of those blitzes come from their linebackers and come straight down the pipe—stressing the A and B gaps. However, teams run outside on Patriots 53.8% of the time (10th highest rate) because their EDGE players are more skilled as pass rushers and can be overwhelmed in the run game. Their vulnerability shows up most in explosive plays. Currently, the Patriots allow an explosive run on 10.9% of rushing attempts (20th), have allowed 22 rushes over 10 yards this season, and average 3.31 yards allowed after contact (24th). When we flip to the Lions' rushing attack, we can see how they match up with the Patriots' weaknesses. The Lions run the ball on the edges 55.7% of the time (7th), lead the NFL in explosive run plays (16.5% of the time), have 33 rushes of 10+ yards (3rd), and average 3.15 yards after contact (10th). If the Patriots blitz and the Lions attack the edge, Jahmyr Gibbs will have a chance to eat. Prediction 2: Goff finds success with quick hitters and deep shots The Patriots' defensive line is built to stop the run up the middle, create pressure off the edge and with blitzing linebackers, then deploy their secondary in nickel sets 77.7% of the time (2nd most in the NFL) and run man coverage out of it 36% of the time (2nd). While chunk yards on the ground will certainly soften the Patriots' defense, Lions quarterback Jared Goff will likely be the key to winning this game because he matches up so well with their coverage scheme. This season, Goff has an EPA of 40.57 vs. nickel defenses (2nd highest in the NFL), a per-play EPA of 0.23 vs. nickel (4th), and a per-play EPA of 0.36 vs. man coverage (3rd). What makes it worse for the Patriots is that their coverage has been exposed in recent weeks, especially by NFC North teams. Last week against the Packers, the Patriots surrendered 372 passing yards to Jordan Love, and 308 to Bears QB Caleb Williams two weeks prior. Those struggles have shown up in their EPA numbers, too. On the season, the Patriots allow a per-pass play EPA of 0.07 (26th), but over the past four weeks, that number has plummeted to 0.35 (31st) Goff's key will be efficiency with short routes and a willingness to test them deep. When the Patriots are in off coverage, use the space against them. When they blitz, having quick-hitter answers in the vacated space behind them will lead to yards after catch (YAC). Then, when success comes underneath with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Sam LaPorta, test them with deep shots to Jameson Williams. Prediction 3: Lions focus on stopping the run; contain Maye As mentioned earlier, the Patriots want to control the game on the ground, but their results haven't matched their dedication. The Patriots run the ball on 46% of offensive plays (10th most) and gain 119.9 yards per game (10th), but their per-play efficiency is more middle-of-the-road. As a team, they average 4.2 yards per rush (14th), but only Drake Maye and RB3 Corey Kiner average above 4.0 yards per carry; RB1 Rhamondre Stevenson and RB2 TreVeyon Henderson average 3.9 yards per carry. We see similar results in EPA and success rate. The team's EPA per run is -0.02 (11th), while Stevenson (-0.06) and Henderson (-0.28) fall below the average. The team's rushing success rate is 41.8% (14th), while Stevenson is close at 40.2, but Henderson is well below at 34.6%. The high volume of run plays can make a middle-of-the-road rushing attack look better than it is, but the real catalyst skewing the numbers is quarterback Drake Maye's mobility. Maye has carried the ball 47 times through nine games, averages 4.7 yards per carry, has a per-play rushing EPA of +0.40, and a 51.1% success rate. Aside from a poor first quarter against Bills QB Josh Allen in Week 2 (when he gained 40 of his 69 rushing yards that day), the Lions defense has done a good job handling mobile quarterbacks this season. Vikings Kyler Murray gained 35 yards in Week 8, but no other quarterback has rushed for 20 yards against the Lions defense: Jacoby Brissett had 19 yards, Geno Smith (12), Tyler Shough (8), Malik Willis (7, groin injury), and Bryce Young (3) were all held under 20 rushing yards. Defenses have deployed a spy on Maye situationally, and I expect the Lions to do the same in this game. Prediction 4: McNeill pressures the middle of the OL The Patriots offensive line has dealt with several injuries this season, and they've struggled to keep pressure at bay. Entering this game, they've allowed 141 pressures (28th) and a 42.9% pressure rate (31st). Maye has done a nice job handling the extra pressure for the most part, only taking 20 sacks (17th) with a 6.6% sack rate (18th), but it has led to him making some poor choices with the football; he is currently tied for the most interceptions in the NFL with 11. So where are the weaknesses in the line? Right up the middle. New England lost both starting guards—Alijah Vera-Tucker and Mike Onwenu—to injured reserve. Backup Greg Van Roten was injured in the one game he started, landed on injured reserve, and has only recently opened his injury evaluation window. Backup center Ben Brown was then called up to shift to guard, but he's been dealing with an injury and has been ruled out for this game. Finally, Walter Rouse has been supplementing/rotating with Brown at left guard, but he is currently in concussion protocol. Heading into this game, Matt Pryor has started at right guard the last three games and is expected to maintain that role, but left guard is still up in the air. The Patriots likely need Rouse to clear concussion protocol or Van Roten to be activated from injured reserve and step into a starting role. Regardless of where they land at left guard, they'll have the unenviable task of trying to block Alim McNeill. McNeill has been a monster this season, as teams have had to deal with the totality of the Lions defensive line. Most teams have focused heavily on Aidan Hutchinson, but the developmental progression of Tyleik Williams, a wonderful rookie season for Skyler Gill-Howard, the steady veteran presence of DJ Wonnum, and the recent emergence of rookie Derrick Moore have allowed McNeill to flourish even more. Through eight games, according to the Lions PR , McNeill is: 1st in games with 0.5 sacks (6) 1st in QB hurries (24) 2nd in total pressures generated (34) 2nd in sacks (5.5) t-4th in QB hits (10) McNeill taking advantage of the reserve guards could be a huge factor in this game. If the Lions rush four and drop seven, and the Patriots need to keep players in for Hutchinson and McNeill, Maye will have fewer targets and a muddied back-seven to sort through. away.headline: A big Munich test for Lions and Patriots as injuries loom for New England
away.blurb: Injuries are a top concern for New England. Before traveling Wednesday night, the Patriots ruled out LG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness). November 12, 2026 / 5:07 PM EST / AP Heading into international games, NFL coaches typically talk up the niceties of "growing the game" globally. The New England Patriots (5-4) have lost two of their past three games and have a slew of injury concerns, including running back Rhamondre Stevenson. The Detroit Lions, even with a 6-2 record and four straight victories, are trying to keep pace in the tight NFC North. Sunday's game in Munich is a big one for both teams. Lions coach Dan Campbell wasn't focused on the international implications. "Well, if I'm being honest, I just haven't thought that far into it. I'm like, 'We've got to get prepared,'" Campbell said. The Patriots were embarrassed at home by the Green Bay Packers last week, losing 45-27, with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions and the secondary struggling to contain the Packers' passing game. Campbell expects a much-improved New England team on Sunday. "You look at the totality of what this team is capable of, the firepower they have, and they're a good team. They're dangerous," he said. "And they're going to clean a lot of things up." The Lions slogged through a 19-9 win over the rebuilding Miami Dolphins last week, relying on four field goals from Jake Bates. It was also just one week after a neck injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell. Detroit's bye week is in the rearview mirror, and after Munich, the team will host Tampa Bay and then Chicago on Thanksgiving Day. "It's a good thing to be tested during the season," Campbell said. "It really is. And to have to go through some of these tough stretches because that's what the playoffs are. That's what it is. And certainly if you got to go on the road. So, that's what this is. This is about us. This is the next obstacle we have. Told the team we're not going to clear it. Our objective is to go through it, and that's the mindset." Stevenson, the team's leading rusher with 399 yards on 102 carries, didn't practice Wednesday because of a knee injury. That could put second-year running back Corey Kiner in line for the bulk of the carries. "Corey has done a really nice job, but there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on," coach Mike Vrabel said, citing "recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure." The coach said "a lot of contending teams" are 5-4. "We've got to start putting ourselves in position to play meaningful games in January or in the middle of January," Vrabel said. "It's usually what happens in the National Football League; a bunch of teams get bunched up, and they go in different directions, and I know the direction that we're going to head in, and that's going to be the one that's forward, positive and winning." The Patriots were embarrassed at home by the Green Bay Packers last week, losing 45-27, with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions and the secondary struggling to contain the Packers' passing game. Campbell expects a much-improved New England team on Sunday. "You look at the totality of what this team is capable of, the firepower they have, and they're a good team. They're dangerous," he said. "And they're going to clean a lot of things up." The Lions slogged through a 19-9 win over the rebuilding Miami Dolphins last week, relying on four field goals from Jake Bates. It was also just one week after a neck injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell. Detroit's bye week is in the rearview mirror, and after Munich, the team will host Tampa Bay and then Chicago on Thanksgiving Day. "It's a good thing to be tested during the season," Campbell said. "It really is. And to have to go through some of these tough stretches because that's what the playoffs are. That's what it is. And certainly if you got to go on the road. So, that's what this is. This is about us. This is the next obstacle we have. Told the team we're not going to clear it. Our objective is to go through it, and that's the mindset." Stevenson, the team's leading rusher with 399 yards on 102 carries, didn't practice Wednesday because of a knee injury. That could put second-year running back Corey Kiner in line for the bulk of the carries. "Corey has done a really nice job, but there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on," coach Mike Vrabel said, citing "recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure." The coach said "a lot of contending teams" are 5-4. "We've got to start putting ourselves in position to play meaningful games in January or in the middle of January," Vrabel said. "It's usually what happens in the National Football League; a bunch of teams get bunched up, and they go in different directions, and I know the direction that we're going to head in, and that's going to be the one that's forward, positive and winning." New England (5-4) vs. Detroit (6-2) in Munich, Germany. When/where to watch: S

home.blurb: Wide receiver A.J. Brown was on hand for it. After missing back-to-back weeks due to a knee issue in addition to the high ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve in September, the former All-Pro returned as a limited participant to begin Detroit Lions prep. But running back TreVeyon Henderson, offensive lineman Ben Brown and cornerback Carlton Davis III stayed among the sidelined in Foxborough and have officially been ruled out for the matchup in Munich. RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness — out) CB Carlton Davis III (knee — out) An illness that kept Henderson hospitalized for multiple days will now keep the running back out for a third straight game. The Patriots will be without another Brown on offense after the team’s starting left guard exited last Sunday’s 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers with a knee injury. And in the secondary, a knee injury will also keep Davis from taking the field in Munich after he’d worked back from a neck injury throughout October. That leaves four non-participants from Wednesday potentially in play for the NFL international series. FB Reggie Gilliam (knee — IR return) G Greg Van Roten (hamstring — IR return) S Kerby Joseph (knee — PUP return) But a pair of 21-day practice windows are now open for New England along with one 53-man roster spot. After Van Roten headed back to practice last week, Gilliam did so to start work on the Lions. The fullback spent the past five games on injured reserve. He marks the fifth IR return designation utilized by New England. NFL rules allot eight per club. Stevenson was a limited participant on Thursday. A.J. Brown, Rhamondre Stevenson among 9 Patriots questionable The team ruled nine players questionable for Week 10, including wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) and running back Rhamondre Stevenson (knee). Brown has not played since Oct. 22 against the Chicago Bears, while Stevenson got banged up last week in the blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers. Brown, who has missed six games out of nine possible in his inaugural season with the Patriots, wasn't ruled out when the team announced offensive lineman Ben Brown (knee), cornerback Carlton Davis (knee), and RB Treveyon Henderson (illness) were inactive for Sunday before they traveled overseas. Brown made the long flight to Germany and was limited in practice all week, a sign he could make his second long-awaited return from his latest ailment. Head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Friday he felt "pretty good" about Brown's chances of suiting up for Week 10 despite his questionable tag. It's good news for Stevenson, whose injury didn't look great and was quickly ruled out after going to the locker room during the Packers matchup. In addition to Brown and Stevenson being questionable, here are the seven others: FB Reggie Gilliam (knee) – designated for return from injured reserve OL Greg Van Roten (hamstring) – designated for return from IR As the Patriots' offensive line woes continue with Ben Brown being ruled out, Vrabel told reporters on Friday he doesn't know who will start at left guard. Greg Van Roten is questionable to be activated from injured reserve as he recovers from a hamstring injury, and Walter Rouse isn't a lock to play as he's in the NFL's concussion protocol. Vrabel said he would have a better idea of who will get the nod following Friday's practice. Rouse was ultimately a limited participant in practice, but Van Roten was a full participant. RB TreVeyon Henderson was ruled out for Week 10 and did not travel with the team as he recovers from a neurological medical emergency. He hasn't played since Oct. 22 and has no timeline for return, but Vrabel offered some insight on the player's situation. "I talk to TreVeyon every day and just like everybody else that's not available, he's working hard to get back and when that is, I don't know," Vrabel said (via MassLive 's Mark Daniels). "I don't have a timetable. But I love my interactions with him, I love talking with him." "We're very conscious of that and we're just until we absolutely need the spot and we haven't had that necessarily pinch and still also just have to try to figure out when he may be available," Vrabel said (via Daniels). KC is looking to build on its blowout win over the Jets in its previous outing. The Falcons have lost four of their past five matchups but aren't technically out of it given the dire state of the NFC South. As a result, Kevin Stefanski's group is viewing this contest as a must-win if they want to stay in the playoff race. Despite Kansas City's impressive 6-2 record, Andy Reid and Co. have dealt with special teams struggles and offensive inconsistencies. Those issues have put a damper on what has otherwise been a successful start. Most analysts view the Chiefs as heavy favorites, but what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor forecast? Chiefs on SI's Take Chiefs fans can only take things one week at a time. Until the Broncos lose and give Kansas City an opening, all the Chiefs can do is beat the opponents in front of them. The biggest storyline of this road clash is the arrival of Josh Downs , who landed with the Chiefs shortly before the trade deadline passed. The shifty slot receiver may not be featured too much out of the gate due to his unfamiliarity with the playbook, but there are bound to be some bright spots in his debut in the red and gold. Kenneth Walker III is a dynamic weapon in the backfield , but Bijan Robinson is on another level. In spite of poor quarterback play, Robinson is virtually unstoppable in the open field and possesses elite vision as a runner. He has three games in which he surpassed 100 yards this season and is averaging 5.2 yards per carry. Atlanta is unsurprisingly a significant underdog coming into this one, though it really depends on which version of the Falcons show up on Sunday. They were blown out by the Bengals last time out and shut out by the Buccaneers a week prior, but they also hold upset victories over the 49ers and Packers. The drastic shifts in Atlanta's play have fans scratching their heads, largely due to the play of quarterback Michael Penix Jr. A week after taking home NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors in Week 7, he tossed a career-high four interceptions and failed to get his team a point. Heading into their final game before a bye, the Falcons are going to throw everything they can at the visiting squad to stay in contention. This is the type of matchup that could see the Chiefs fall into an early deficit if they aren't careful. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Both the Chiefs (6-2) and the Falcons (3-6) meet Sunday afternoon in Atlanta. They are each within one half-game of first place in their respective divisions. The Broncos lead Kansas City in the AFC West while the Falcons are looking up at the Panthers and the Saints in the NFC South. This despite Atlanta having lost two in a row and the Chiefs two of their last three. Kansas City is coming off a convincing 35-12 win over the New York Jets, a game that turned after the Chiefs trailed 12-7 in the second quarter. Patrick Mahomes completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns, both scoring passes going to Kenneth Walker III , who was the offensive centerpiece with 102 rushing yards, 143 yards from scrimmage and three total touchdowns. Travis Kelce added 72 receiving yards and even scored on a one-yard run. The defense took over after halftime, holding New York scoreless in the final thirty minutes as the Chiefs pulled away with 21 unanswered second-half points. Kansas City also went 4-for-4 in the red zone, an encouraging development after back-to-back losses to Seattle and Denver. Mahomes did briefly leave the field after hurting his arm/elbow on a strip-sack but returned and finished the game. As a result, the injury report is worth following as gametime approaches. Atlanta, meanwhile, returns home after a disappointing 34-17 loss to Cincinnati in Madrid, its second straight defeat following a 16-0 shutout loss at Tampa Bay. The Falcons opened strongly against the Bengals with an 80-yard drive resulting in a Michael Penix Jr. touchdown pass to Charlie Woerner . The scoring continued as they took a 10-7 lead later in the first quarter, but Cincinnati answered with 17 unanswered points in the second quarter and Atlanta never recovered. Penix finished 20-of-31 for 162 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Bijan Robinson supplied the offense’s biggest bright spot with 100 rushing yards and a touchdown on 19 carries. Drake London caught five passes for 68 yards, but Atlanta committed 12 penalties for 88 yards and allowed Joe Burrow to throw three touchdown passes. The central storyline from Atlanta’s perspective is will they be able to control the ball and keep Mahomes and co. off the field? The Falcons average 138.8 yards rushing per game. For Kansas City, it is about limiting Bijan Robinson and Atlanta’s rushing attack. The Chiefs have thrived against the run to date this season allowing just 96.3 yards on the ground per game. These teams last met two seasons ago. Mercedes-Benz Stadium was the site and Kansas City won 22-17. Mahomes threw for 217 yards and two touchdowns, while Rashee Rice caught 12 passes for 110 yards and a score; Atlanta, then quarterbacked by Kirk Cousins , had a chance late but could not complete the comeback. Let’s dive further into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. away.headline: Chiefs' Kenneth Walker listed as questionable against Falcons after late injury report addition
away.blurb: Chiefs' Kenneth Walker has been listed as questionable for game against Falcons According to the official Kansas City injury report, star running back Kenneth Walker did not practice Friday and is being listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons . Who steps up if Kenneth Walker is unavailable? Kansas City would benefit from Walker being available, but the offense should still be able to perform well enough to win if he is forced to miss the game. Vikings rookie Jakobe Thomas speaks out after giving up No. 8 jersey for Kirk Cousins A late addition to Friday's injury report for the Kansas City Chiefs could be worrisome come kickoff on Sunday. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid revealed that Walker arrived at the team facility Friday with a groin injury that caused him to miss practice. It will now become a waiting game for Kansas City, as it likely won't have a good understanding of Walker's availability until just ahead of kickoff on Sunday. Walker has been outstanding in his first season with the Chiefs, ranking second in the NFL in rushing yards (872) and tied for ninth in rushing touchdowns (7). He's already set a career high in receiving touchdowns (4) and is on pace to set a new career high in receiving yards. If in fact Walker is unable to play on Sunday, Kansas City would turn to backup running back Emmett Johnson for the bulk of the carries. He may not be featured much, though, as the Chiefs could very well try to attack the Falcons defense through the air. There is a path to victory that way, as Atlanta ranks 20th in passing yards allowed (228.0), 20th in passing touchdowns allowed (20) and 29th in interceptions (3). It is evident that the Falcons struggle defending the pass, something the Chiefs may have to exploit with a solid passing attack. Want more articles like this? And it's a game for the Texans that'll be extremely important to take advantage of. They'll be taking the road trying to climb one game closer to .500, face up against another AFC Wild Card contender, and will be trying to build upon the 44-point outing they saw last weekend against the LA Chargers. So what can we expect from the Texans in this game against the Browns? Will they rise to the occasion for a second straight win, or fall into similar pitfalls that they have in their five losses so far this season? Well, let's sort through a batch of three bold predictions for the Texans to take our chances at guessing how things will unravel in Cleveland on Sunday: 1. The Browns, while they haven't allowed 30 points to an opponent dating back to Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, have certainly gotten close a few times. And on top of that, they haven't really played a high-powered offense like the Texans many times this season. If the Texans can keep their momentum through the air and the offense can continue to limit the penalties setting them back as they did last weekend, 30 points is wildly possible for this team. So far this season, the Browns are 0-1 in games where they allow 30 points or more, and have yet to score 30 points a game themselves. This might be a simple recipe for Houston's success this weekend. 2. That becomes clear when looking at Houston's interception totals in the secondary. Not one player has recorded more than one interception on the season so far. In all, the Texans' defense has just four interceptions, which makes them one of nine teams in the NFL to log four or fewer interceptions on the season thus far. It's a result that needs to turn around in the right direction for Houston in the second half of their schedule for this defense to be at it's true elite potential. The Browns are 3-0 at home this year, but after having lost two straight games, they are being treated like an afterthought this week. As you can see in the national picks below, not a single person is picking the Browns at home. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 10 game between the Browns and Texans: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Texans: Even sitting at 3-5, the Texans appear to be full steam ahead toward a playoff berth with the way their offense is playing and defense is improving. C.J. Stroud has Nick Caley's unit absolutely humming now that most of his main targets are healthy. The real key to that success is Nico Collins. In the 257 snaps Collins has played this season, the Texans have averaged 8.2 yards per passing play, more than the 49ers' league-leading 7.9. He could be stalled when matched up against cornerback Denzel Ward, who's allowing 0.5 yards per coverage snap, fifth-fewest among cornerbacks (min. 150 coverage snaps). That duel is sure to be dogfight Sunday, but no matter, as I have faith in Stroud's other weapons (Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr., Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson) to get it done. Houston's lone offensive weakness matches up nicely against the Browns' permeable run defense. Getting Deshaun Watson back is a boost for Cleveland, but even with him, the Browns have struggled to put together a full game, instead relying on a few big plays each week from their young stars. An all-around performance is exactly what the Browns must have to beat the current version of DeMeco Ryans' team. Thus, Cleveland will fall short of improving to 4-0 at home for the first time since the 1963 campaign, when Jim Brown led the NFL in rushing and scrimmage yards in a 14-game season. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Texans 21, Browns 20 This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won't matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns. But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Texans 24, Browns 16 Anyway, this genuinely does feel like a game that's going to boil down to Watson vs. the Texans. Watson has been sacked more times than any other QB in the NFL this year (33), and he'll be facing a defense that leads the NFL in sacks (29). That's a recipe for disaster. There have only been three games all season where a QB has been sacked at least eight times: Two of them were Deshaun Watson (vs. Jets in Week 5 and vs. Steelers in Week 8) and the other one happened on Sunday with the Texans sacking Justin Herbert eight times. Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Texans 20, Browns 17 The Texans hope to sneak back into the playoff picture and their defense got back to making big plays in Los Angeles after the bye. Cleveland's defense will get a break as Houston is one-dimensional out of necessity, but in the end, old Texans friend Deshaun Watson will be outdueled by red-hot C.J. Stroud. Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud is coming off a 384-yard, five-TD performance against the Chargers. The Browns' early-season shine is wearing off, but they are 4-0 ATS as an underdog of seven points or less. Currently sitting at 3-5, the Texans must get back to their winning ways long-term if they plan on making a postseason push in the AFC. Right now, no one should be talking about the playoffs, especially since Houston has blown three fourth-quarter leads and remains winless at home. The good news? Sunday's matchup is on the road, a place where Houston is 3-1. The Texans will travel to Cleveland for a date with Deshaun Watson and the Browns in Week 10. Cleveland, which could be gunning for a wild-card berth under first-year coach Todd Monken, fell short on Sunday in a battle down in the bayou amid an overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints . Cleveland plans to start Watson, Houston's former franchise quarterback, but second-year passer Shedeur Sanders proved his potential by keeping the Browns alive in the Superdome. Despite a slow offensive start, Houston found a rhythm in the second quarter and never looked back. The Texans could be dealing with a multitude of injuries following Friday's practice. For the third straight day, rookie offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge did not practice. Running back Woody Marks and defensive ends Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter also could be in trouble after missing practice on Thursday and Friday. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Houston Texans (3-5) head to Cleveland on Sunday looking to continue a dramatic midseason turnaround when they face the Browns (5-4) at Huntington Bank Field. The Texans opened the season with four straight losses but have won three of their last four. The division may be out of reach as the Jaguars lead the Texans by three games in the AFC South but Houston is back in the race for a Wild Card spot. Cleveland takes the field after dropping their last two games which has dropped them out of first in the AFC North and 1.5 games behind the Steelers and the Bengals. Houston is coming off its most explosive performance of the season, a 44-22 road rout of the winless Los Angeles Chargers. C.J. Stroud played through an illness and completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception. He connected with four different players for scores, including 63-yard touchdowns to Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte , with Boutte finishing with 125 receiving yards and two touchdowns. The Texans led 24-9 at halftime, stretched the advantage to 38-9 early in the fourth quarter and defensively overwhelmed Justin Herbert , sacking him eight times. Cleveland arrives home following a gut-wrenching 23-22 overtime loss at New Orleans. With Deshaun Watson sidelined by a concussion, Shedeur Sanders started and finished 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns, including a 64-yard go-ahead strike to KC Concepcion late in the fourth quarter. After New Orleans regained the lead, Andre Szmyt’s 51-yard field goal forced overtime. The Saints scored first in the extra period, but Sanders answered by finding Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown before Cleveland went for two and the win; the conversion failed, dropping the Browns to 5-4. The matchup also renews a surprisingly balanced series. Houston leads the all-time matchup 8-7, including the postseason, but Cleveland won four consecutive meetings from 2020 through the 2023 regular season. Their most recent clash reversed that trend in emphatic fashion: in the 2023 AFC Wild Card round, Stroud threw for 274 yards and three touchdowns as Houston demolished Cleveland 45-14, with the Texans turning two Joe Flacco interceptions into defensive touchdowns. In addition to Watson’s health, other storylines include the Texans’ pass rush against Cleveland’s quarterback protection particularly after Sanders was sacked five times in New Orleans and Houston just recorded eight sacks against the Chargers. Let’s dive further into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. Yet, the biggest and perhaps most surprising absence that Houston will be faced with this weekend surrounds their veteran star edge rusher Danielle Hunter, who's been ruled out after logging a limited practice on Thursday and didn't participate on Friday. All we know is that Hunter likely suffered a hamstring injury during practice on Thursday, and it's serious enough to keep him out for one week–– and possibly more, knowing that the Texans are on a short week for Week 11. Azeez Al-Shaair is out for the Texans once again, seemingly with another groin injury that's kept him limited throughout the past several weeks . Another noteworthy name from the Texans' lineup who won't be playing on Sunday: their big trade acquisition of Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), who was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, but would not suit up for Thursday or Friday. And knowing that Harrison Jr. is dealing with a hamstring issue, there's a possibility that the Texans' wideout suffered that hamstring tweak in the middle of Houston's team session on Wednesday, and will now be forced out for a period of time. Montgomery's case is simple: he's been dealing with a groin injury dating back to Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans, has been out for the past three games, but was a full practice participant on Friday, that gives him hope to finally get back on the field for Week 10. However, for Anderson Jr., he deserves a bit more attention for his situation. He was a limited participant in practice on Thursday due to an ankle issue, and would inevitably not practice on Friday as a DNP. home.headline: Texans injury update: RB Woody Marks could miss Week 10 vs. Browns
home.blurb: The Houston Texans already have a limited running game with Woody Marks taking a majority of their carries. The Texans could be without both David Montgomery and Marks following Thursday's injury report. Marks, who was not out at practice, was listed as limited with a knee injury on Thursday. Texans injury update: RB Woody Marks could miss Week 10 vs. Browns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Texans injury update: RB Woody Marks could miss Week 10 vs. Browns Cole Thompson, Texans Wire · Texans Wire Fri, November 13, 2026 at 8:49 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads What about having zero running game in Week 10 against the Cleveland Browns ? This is massive since Montgomery, the Texans' top running back in Week 1, has not played since the victory over the Tennessee Titans last month with a groin injury. Plus, given that the Texans waived running back Dare Ogunbowale earlier this week, the only running back left on the roster who's nearly 100 percent is Emari Demercado. Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley said that while Demercado hasn't seen an extensive amount of reps, running back's coach Danny Barrett always has someone locked in and ready to go. "Just getting them all ready, giving them opportunities and being conscientious of monitoring reps, who's gotten what reps, who hasn't, making sure we can get guys reps, really trying to format roles as the week goes on to allow those guys to just hone in and get time on task in specific things," Caley said. "We've got a good group of guys that all are there to support each other. Just trying to build it throughout the week and take it day by day, really." The Texans, who ranked 29th in rushing, could be in line for a strong day on the ground against Cleveland's defensive line. While the Browns have been successful in creating a pass rush, they rank 27th against the run, allowing 130.6 yards per game and 4.7 yards per run. Last week, Marks rushed for 70 yards on 12 carries and had his longest run of the season in a 44-22 win over the Chargers. Kickoff is scheduled for Noon on FOX. home.headline: Texans Injury Report vs. Browns Week 10: Multiple Starters Miss Practice
home.blurb: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans made it known that Montgomery's status has improved from last week ––when he was ruled out with a groin injury on Wednesday––but said he would continue to be evaluated throughout the week. It remains to be seen if he ends up playing once the weekend rolls around. Azeez Al-Shaair might be a name to keep an eye on, as he was a DNP with seemingly the same groin injury that's restricted his availability in practice as of late . However, given that he also had a personal designation, there's a better chance that he'll be good to go for either Thursday or Friday's session. Tight end Brevin Jordan also wound up as a DNP in practice with a finger/foot issue. If he's unable to go against the Browns, Houston has four other tight ends on the roster to turn to instead, including second-round rookie Marlin Klein, who was active on the gameday against the LA Chargers for the first time since Week 4. The Texans' final status for everyone on the roster will become clearer after Friday's practice. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense. … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) (SNF) Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. Pittsburgh always seems to be right in the thick of it in these division games, and the first matchup was decided by only three points. I think the scoring margin is the same here, but with slightly lower scoring, in keeping with the trend of divisional rematches. … Prediction: Bengals 23, Steelers 20 Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) (MNF) Dajani ( Chargers +4.5): This is potentially the worst Monday night game of all time. A winless team that hasn't covered the spread since last year vs. a spiraling team starting a new quarterback. Jacoby Brissett is an upgrade over Joe Fagnano , but how much of an upgrade immediately? I don't have a great read on this matchup, but I'll take Jim Harbaugh to keep things close with his brother's old team. … Prediction: Ravens 20, Chargers 17 Dubin (Chargers +4.5): I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. LA's offense is pretty broken, but the Ravens haven't exactly been great defensively (25th in scoring defense), so the Chargers might be able to put at least some points on the board. … Prediction: Ravens 24, Chargers 20 Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Da

Now, the two teams will conclude their regular-season series with a chilly match at Lambeau Field. Vikings fans are still riding the excitement from a major adrenaline injection early this week as the team reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins via trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. What once looked like a potential beatdown in Green Bay now looks like a massive opportunity for the Vikings to end a two-game losing streak and sweep their biggest rival. There’s still a lot up in the air, especially since head coach Kevin O’Connell hasn't technically named Cousins the starter yet. Justin Jefferson returns to form (for real this time) Frick it, Justin Jefferson is down there somewhere. There is perhaps no larger beneficiary of the Cousins’ reunion tour than Jefferson. While many had assumed star pass rusher Micah Parsons would be back by now, the Vikings have the distinct advantage of avoiding him in both regular-season matchups. Two of these teams will miss the playoffs pic.twitter.com/7VewNM4oiT With a reenergized offense, a motivated Cousins returning to the scene of a career-altering injury, and O’Connell in “prove it” mode, I think we finally see a well-rounded 2026 Vikings squad in action. Yet, after losing back-to-back games, the Vikings know they can reach a higher ceiling, because they were in first place for the first seven weeks of the season. The hope is that trading for Kirk Cousins can resurrect Kevin O’Connell’s previously potent scoring attacks after ranking just 27th in points this season. Yet, considering the four-time Pro Bowl QB has already operated Kevin O’Connell’s offense for two seasons, it shouldn’t take the 38-year-old long to get back in the saddle. Even though he was just acquired Tuesday, Cousins understands the importance of the Vikings’ next matchup, against the division rival Green Bay Packers, who enter the week at 6-3, in fourth place of the division. As Sunday approaches, it’s time to dive into four bold predictions for this week’s Vikings-Packers game. Yet, Jefferson already has chemistry with Cousins, and the new Vikings QB is playing at an elite level.
