picks.blurb: Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football FAA ground stop updates Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Justis Mosqueda · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 6:40 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers (6-3) are set to be three-point favorites over the Minnesota Vikings (6-1) in Week 10, according to FanDuel's numbers . That number comes with a little juice at -120, and the Packers are -178 favorites, which comes with an implied probability of 64 percent. If you had said this a few weeks ago, when the Packers' offensive line was drowning, no one would have bought it. Now, after Green Bay finally had a 100-yard rushing performance and beat down on the New England Patriots in all three phases of the game, it looks like the Packers have a real opportunity to make a push for the postseason. The Vikings have played two fewer games than the Packers because: 1) they've already had their bye week and 2) they're playing on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. After that game, they'll have a short(er) week and have to travel on the road to Lambeau Field. Their starting quarterback, Kyler Murray, is currently dealing with a hamstring injury and will not play against the Bills. We'll have to see if it heals up by the time they kick off against the Packers, or if it'll be Carson Wentz — their current replacement starter — under center. The only other quarterback in Minnesota is Max Brosmer (53-man roster). Below is the current playoff picture in the NFC: San Francisco 49ers: 7-1 (NFC West) Minnesota Vikings: 6-1 (NFC North) New York Giants: 5-2-1 (NFC East) Carolina Panthers: 3-5 (NFC South) Chicago Bears: 7-2 Detroit Lions: 6-2 Green Bay Packers: 6-3 Seattle Seahawks: 5-4 Los Angeles Rams: 5-4 Dallas Cowboys: 4-5 New Orleans Saints: 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 3-6 Atlanta Falcons: 3-6 Arizona Cardinals: 3-6 Washington Commanders: 2-5-1 Philadelphia Eagles: 2-7 The Packers are holding onto the seventh seed right now, where they've been for weeks, but the NFC North keeps winning — as do the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams, the teams trying to hunt them down from behind. The NFC is so wonky, with the "good" teams being in the North and West, not the South and East, that the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers currently have about as good a chance of making the playoffs (by winning the NFC South) as do the Los Angeles Rams (a .500 team that is essentially locked into a playoff spot or nothing in 2026), per The Athletic's playoff simulator . In short, there are seven North and West teams fighting for five playoff spots in the NFC, and then there's whatever the hell is happening in the East and South. Do not be surprised at all if a sub-.500 NFC South team ends up hosting a 12-5 (or better record) NFC North team in the wild card round this year.

picks.headline: Week 10 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Kirk Cousins returns to lead Vikings vs. Packers
picks.blurb: Week 10 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Kirk Cousins returns to lead Vikings vs. Packers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football FAA ground stop updates Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Frank Schwab Senior writer Fri, November 13, 2026 at 6:08 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It wasn't that long ago that Kirk Cousins, in his first stint with the Minnesota Vikings, was the quarterback who could never win the big one . Everyone remembers this critique of him. These days, Kirk Cousins is 38. And somehow, everyone spent days and weeks arguing that the only way for the Vikings to have a chance to win the big one was to trade for Cousins. That trade did happen, and it was perfectly reasonable for the Vikings to see if Cousins can guide them to an NFC North title and maybe a playoff run. They have the defense for it but we saw on Monday night that the offense was beyond repair with the quarterback situation they had. Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was hesitant to announce Cousins would start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers, but the Vikings didn't trade for Cousins to watch Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz start in a huge divisional game. While the trade for Cousins was reasonable, the Vikings still have the fourth-best quarterback in the division and the fourth-best offense in the division as well. Cousins is an upgrade but mostly because the Vikings had a dreadful quarterback situation. The Packers didn't do anything at the trade deadline but it might be because they've been on quite a roll. They were not good through three weeks but somehow have emerged as one of the better teams in the NFL since then. Since Week 4, they're fourth in EPA ( expected points added ) per play on offense and third in EPA per play allowed on defense. It's a good team. Anyone will have issues with the Vikings' defense and we'll see if the Packers' deep passing game can function against Minnesota's many blitzes. But Packers -3 is the pick. Taking the Vikings and Cousins, five days after rejoining the team, against a red-hot team is too much to ask. New Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) shown facing the Packers in a 2023 game. Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 10 of the NFL season: Patriots (+2.5) over Lions This is the NFL's last early-morning game of the season. The Lions and Patriots meet in Germany. The Patriots are coming off a bad loss to the Packers, and have their running back issues with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson out. One factor to consider is the Lions aren't the same team outdoors. Jared Goff's rating in domes is 102.9 and outdoors it is 92.4. There is some noise in those numbers, and Goff's ratings haven't had that big of a gap the past two seasons, but Detroit also just scored 19 points at Miami last week. That and the Lions' defensive deficiencies are enough to take the Patriots and the points. Texans (-4.5) over Browns The Browns have a better record, but also a -35 point differential. It's not like the Texans have been great, but there's a path for them to make the playoffs. They also know they can't drop games like this one. C.J. Stroud is playing well enough that points shouldn't be too hard for Houston to come by. Titans (+10.5) over Jaguars The Jaguars have taken over as my Super Bowl pick after the deadline. However, 10.5 is a lot of points in the NFL and the Titans have played three close games in a row. They're coming off their bye and have some extra rest. The Jaguars can't blow everyone out, right? Colts (-3.5) over Dolphins It's very hard to take the Colts, especially because the Dolphins are playing hard. The Colts played hard last week, but have to be deflated after losing that game to the Cowboys in the final minutes and seeing more players traded away. But it's even harder to back new Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord, a 2025 sixth-round pick who has never taken an NFL snap, playing with a subpar group. McCord gets the start for Miami with Malik Willis on injured reserve. Jets (+8) over Bills Talk about an ugly NFL side to take. The Jets are not good. But the Bills are coming off a physical game in Minnesota on Monday night and now go on the road to face the Jets on short rest. It seems unwise to take the Jets, but point spreads exist for a reason. Panthers (+2.5) over Saints The Saints are probably better in theory than reality. They won last week, but needed to defend a two-point conversion in overtime to knock off Shedeur Sanders and the Browns. It feels like the Saints have the potential to be the best team in the NFC South, but there's not much evidence they are. The Panthers are in a slump but have been the better team. Chiefs (-3.5) over Falcons It's not like the Falcons trading Jessie Bates III makes them significantly worse, but it's a difficult message for the locker room. It makes it seem like the front office is waving the white flag. In reality they got an offer they couldn't turn down, but it's still worth wondering how the remaining players will react. And Kansas City is a pretty good team. Cardinals (+9.5) over Rams For the rest of the season, or at least until Puka Nacua or Davante Adams returns, the Rams will try to survive by running the ball and playing defense in low-scoring games. There's not much explosiveness in the offense without any dangerous receivers. That will make them tough to back when the spread is large. Can Carson Beck lead the Arizona offense to enough points against a good Rams defense to cover any spread? That's the key question. Seahawks (-6.5) over Raiders This isn't a pick due to Fernando Mendoza facing the Seahawks defense, though that is a factor. It's because the Raiders defense is horrible. Since Week 3, after the Raiders had faced the offensively challenged Dolphins and Chargers, they're last in the NFL in EPA by a wide margin. They're 32nd in yards allowed and points allowed. The Seahawks will be able to move the ball, even with Drew Lock at quarterback. 49ers (-4.5) over Cowboys There are no signs the Cowboys are ready to have some kind of breakout. Last week they almost lost to a Colts team that has already given up on the season. And now they're supposed to keep it close against the 49ers, who have arguably been the best team in the NFL? Steelers (+3.5) over Bengals The Joe Burrow-for-MVP bandwagon is still running , but it's hard to lay more than a field goal in what should be a great divisional game. The Steelers can run the ball, and run defense is a weakness of the Bengals. They're last in the NFL in yards allowed per carry. Also, the Steelers are coming off a bye while the Bengals are coming off a game in Paris, which is the type of massive rest disadvantage that the NFL should do a better job avoiding. The Bengals are good but this isn't a great matchup or a good spot for them. Ravens (-4.5) over Chargers The Chargers will cover a spread this season. They haven't yet. They are the last team in the NFL to not cover the spread this season. But we'll take that loss when it comes because proactively taking the truly miserable Chargers in hopes they finally cover is not an enjoyable exercise. Also, the Ravens have three days of extra rest and perhaps a little bit of renewed hope with Jacoby Brissett coming aboard. This week: 1-0 Last week: 9-6 Season to date: 63-71-2

away.headline: Senior NFL insider has high hopes for Vikings following Kirk Cousins trade
away.blurb: He also pointed out how Cousins just immediately took charge from day one of returning to his former team. Related Articles NFL Insider Explains Ravens’ Lamar Jackson Return Window Let us be frank: The moment the world heard that Kirk Cousins would be returning to the Minnesota Vikings mere hours before Tuesday’s trade deadline, there was a sigh of relief from fans that was so loud, it broke the sound barrier. So, naturally, insiders and professionals alike are weighing in about how the rest of the Vikings season can look with Cousins back in the driver’s seat, including NFL senior insider Ian Rapoport. “I feel like if they can just play like, average offense, and they should be better than that, but if they can play average offense, this becomes one of the best teams in the NFL because their defense is so good,” Rapoport said on “The Pat McAfee Show” on Friday when asked how big Cousins’ first game back against the Green Bay Packers will be. “And that’s what I kind of liked about this move for the Vikings is they clearly feel like because their defense is so good, we have an opportunity, we have to seize it. Whatever it costs, like, whatever happens, it’s like get a viable quarterback and just get this thing rolling. You know, they now get a boost for the second half of the year. “I think Cousins is going to hit the ground running. It’s an incredible opportunity to bring back someone who has been in the system, who they loved, who is playing really good football at 38-years-old like, this is an excellent situation for the Minnesota Vikings.” What makes a huge difference is Minnesota is where Cousins wants to be and where his teammates and coaches want him to be. Especially receiver Justin Jefferson, who said that welcoming Cousins back was a “joy.” “He just understands the game,” Jefferson said, ESPN reported . “He’s a guy that studies the game a lot. He understands how the defenses play, especially covering me. And he understands, the plays that we have called that are kind of my plays and he understands the timing and the windows to throws those type of plays, but he also doesn’t force those type of plays to me and he just lets the game come to me.” “He’s being vocal,” Jefferson continued. “Just making sure that everybody hears the plays that he’s talking about and the notes that he has for certain routes, certain plays. And he’s just making sure that everybody’s on the same page. So it’s definitely cool to hear that type of leadership and command. If you know Kirk, that’s pretty normal from him. So it’s definitely kind of cool him being back in that room and him taking control.” Why Ja’Marr Chase Brought Up the Chiefs Ahead of Bengals–Steelers Showdown Lions HC Dan Campbell Reveals Major Drake Maye Concern Before Patriots Clash Start your unlimited Newsweek trial

away.headline: Vikings-Bills Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray is out as expected, as are both Demond Claiborne and Jauan Jennings. Claiborne suffered a knee injury in practice and from Kevin O’Connell’s comments on Saturday, could be out for a while. It wouldn’t be surprising therefore if he was placed on Injured Reserve. It doesn’t appear at the moment that Jennings’ calf injury is a longer-term concern, but we may learn more about that next week. Beyond that, safeties Theo Jackson and Jay Ward are questionable for Monday night. I’m guessing at least one of them will play, but KOC also talked about potentially having Jacob Thomas and/or Tavierre Thomas on the active roster for Monday night to fill in at safety and special teams. For the Bills, backup wide receiver Joshua Palmer is out. But they also have two starting offensive linemen listed as questionable- left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson. Dawkins has not practiced all week with a rib injury, so he would seem to be less likely than normal to start with that designation. Anderson was upgraded to limited on Saturday after missing Thursday and Friday practices with an ankle injury. My guess is that if either of them play on Monday night they will be less than 100%, so the left side of the Bills’ offensive line could be a bit more vulnerable than normal. Beyond that, Tyrell Shavers and Jordan Hancock are listed as questionable, but the Bills will need to activate them from the PUP list and IR for them to be eligible to play on Monday night. We’ll see if that happens. home.headline: Packers-Vikings Wednesday Injury Report: Huge List Filled With Big Names
home.blurb: Officially, the Packers did not practice on Wednesday as they get ready for Sunday’s showdown against the Minnesota Vikings. If they would have, five starters would not have practiced and a total of 16 players were dealing with one issue or another. Rhyan was injured during the opening series at Detroit. So, he missed most of that game and then the next two games. Coach Matt LaFleur said Rhyan could “potentially” return this week, but that he would not have practiced on Wednesday might not be a good sign for Sunday. The questions on the offensive line run deeper than center. Left guard Aaron Banks (knee/hip) would have been limited participation, a continuation of a season filled with injuries. He’s played only 137 snaps. Of his three starts, he was unable to go the distance against the Jets in Week 2 or the Patriots last week. When Banks was knocked out of the New England game, Kevin Zeitler made his Packers debut. Well, he would have been limited participation, as well, with an ankle injury. Linebacker Ty’Ron Hopper, who played only two defensive snaps vs. the Patriots due to a pregame chest injury, would have been limited due to illness; the chest is not mentioned on the injury report. Kicker Trey Smack (right calf) and receiver Savion Williams (groin) were listed as limited participation, as well. Skyy Moore Designated for Return Receiver Skyy Moore was designated for return after missing the last four games with an ankle injury. He is averaging 16.0 yards per punt return, highlighted by a 63-yarder against the Jets, and 27.5 yards per kickoff return. Both figures lead the team. Running back Chris Brooks (ankle) and edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), who are entering their second week of practice after being designated for return, would have been limited. Brooks would be a big addition against the Vikings’ blitzing defense. Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/hip), RB Chris Brooks (ankle), G/T Travis Glover (knee), LB Ty’Ron Hopper (illness), WR Skyy Moore (ankle), edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), K Trey Smack (right calf), WR Savion Williams (groin), G Kevin Zeitler (ankle). Note: Brooks, Moore and Parsons have been designated to return and are within their 21-day practice window. Limited participation: S Jay Ward (knee), QB Carson Wentz (ankle). home.headline: Vikings-Packers Second Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, no change in injury status for anybody compared to Wednesday’s estimates. That doesn’t bode well for any of the players that have yet to practice this week being available on Sunday. We’ll see if there are any upgrades tomorrow, but otherwise it looks like in addition to Blake Cashman, Hockenson, Ingram-Dawkins, Jennings, and Van Noy may not be available on Sunday. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- After a frantic start to the week that saw the Jacksonville Jaguars make the biggest moves of this year's NFL Trade Deadline, it is worth remember that the Jaguars do, in fact, have an opponent on Sunday. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. Two out of the next three weeks, the Titans stand in the way. FOX Sports already had Jacksonville listed as a top 10 defensive team in the NFL prior to these trades. If Tennessee falls short (as is likely expected), it will be because the Jaguars' defense put a stopper in Ward and the offense's growth. That could be one reason among many, but it seems to be the most relevant by far regarding this specific matchup. Prediction: Titans lose, 34-23 At the end of the day on Sunday, I expect Jacksonville will overwhelm Tennessee. I don't believe it will be in blowout fashion, and this is primarily because of the stable flashes of progress Ward showed in Week 8. But between their overhauled defense and Trevor Lawrence manning things under center on offense, the Titans are truly facing a championship contender this week. Perhaps the home field will help blunt the blow, as well as the team debuting their Music City jerseys. I love the jerseys. I like what we saw from Cam Ward in his most recent game. But this Jaguars team has the AFC South in a headlock, and the 1-7 Titans simply don't have enough on paper to climb out of a double-digit projected loss in this one. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Gus Logue · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 6:15 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Welcome to Big Cat Country's staff roundtable! This week, we're recapping the Jacksonville Jaguars' moves at the 2026 NFL trade deadline and previewing their Week 10 divisional matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Question 1: What are your thoughts on the Jaguars' moves at the 2026 trade deadline? Dillon Appleman : I love the moves, and while I understand the outside criticism regarding traditional thoughts on trade value, we know by now that James Gladstone's roster-building philosophy doesn't operate within conventional guardrails. Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis don't just plug the holes left by Eric Murray and DaVon Hamilton; they provide genuine ceiling-raisers for a deep playoff run alongside Davon Godchaux, who adds needed interior depth. In a wide-open AFC, it's now or never, and I'm fired up that this front office is treating it like "now." Travis Holmes : The regime consistently claimed that they would be bold. They were hired to be aggressive in that regard while ushering in a new day in Jacksonville. They have certainly been bold, walking the fine line between calculated aggression and recklessness. The trade for Bates was, in my estimation, a franchise-altering move for Anthony Campanile's defensive scheme. Godchaux providing additional interior defensive line depth for the low cost of a 2028 sixth is the cherry on top of what was already a fantastic class, headlined by the clear jewel, Davis. Personally, I loved the bold moves. Getting value back in trades is great when you're already a perennial powerhouse. You know what's even cooler, though? Becoming a powerhouse in the first place. Gus Logue : I had the same reaction to the draft-day trade for Travis Hunter. Was it an overpay on paper? Sure. Can I guarantee that the acquired player(s) will ball out for Jacksonville? No way. In both cases, Gladstone took a major risk — but it comes with massive upside. The Jaguars could have the NFL's most valuable non-quarterback, and now, maybe the first pro sports championship in Duval County. This franchise has been in the gutter for most of my life, but I don't want them to just aim for ground level. Kudos to the Jaguars for shooting for the stars. Henry Zimmer : The Jaguars went all in, and it makes sense. James Gladstone comes from the Les Sneed tree of not valuing draft capital if it means hanging a banner. And banners hang forever. The Jags took big swings but paid a solid price, so now they have to make good on those deals and win the whole thing. Question 2: Are you ready to set Super Bowl expectations for the Jaguars? Dillon : Not quite. As much as I'd love to let expectations fly with how dominant this team looks, I'm keeping both feet on the ground for now. After last year's disappointing Wild Card exit, I need to see this group prove they can sustain this level of execution on the postseason stage before I'm ready to stamp them with Super Bowl expectations. Travis : You don't have to get ready if you stay ready. Some of us have been waiting for the day when we could finally set those expectations for the Jacksonville Jaguars organization. The literal night of the Jaguars' playoff comeback against the Chargers, I stated the second-half victory would set the franchise back another two to three years by holding onto Trent Baalke and Doug Pederson, despite the fact that it seemed clear neither was forward-thinking in the way necessary to succeed in today's NFL. The goal was always Super Bowl or bust, in my mind. The 2026 Jacksonville Jaguars have finally joined the rest of the modern NFL. Hell yeah. Gus : While it's inaccurate to say Jacksonville went "all in" at the trade deadline, their moves were certainly in the "win now" category. They recognize the opportunity that lies ahead. I understand that some scarred Jaguars fans will be wary of setting expectations too high — and it's wiser to enjoy the present path than overthink the destination — but I also think it'd be healthy for us to start talking about the Big Game. I don't want to reach the AFC Championship and still be thinking, "I don't know, do they really have what it takes?" The Jags aren't all in on this one season… but I am. Henry : Whether we like it or not, by way of the trade deadline, you have to set Super Bowl expectations for Jacksonville. I worry a bit that this has gone a step too far and the Jags are not really the Super Bowl stratosphere but we have to expect them to be of that class. One home playoff game later and here we are! Question 3: Who will be an X-factor for the Jaguars this week against the Titans? Dillon : My X-factor this week is Parker Washington. Despite some big plays here and there, Washington has been held to under 5 receptions in five of his last six games. While much of that quiet stretch comes down to Jacksonville's deep stable of pass catchers and a thriving ground game, Washington has also left a few plays on the field recently. Against a vulnerable Titans secondary, I'm betting he breaks out for another signature performance that has Duval tweeting "PAY THE MAN" on Sunday. Travis : A.J. Brown? Derrick Henry? Jeffery Simmons? For a scrappy Tennessee Titans team that is clearly a shell of its former self, this one ultimately comes down to quarterback Cam Ward's ability to extend plays and find the open receiver early and on time. This Titans offense is clearly hitting its stride, scoring 24, 26, and 36 points over the past three weeks of regulation. Over that three-game stretch, Cam is averaging just 196 yards per game with 1 touchdown and 1 turnover in each matchup, and a 61% completion rate. However, his ability to extend plays while scrambling has been invaluable in keeping this Titans passing offense on schedule and on the field over the past three weeks. Gus : Bates and Davis are taking a personal bye week against the Titans. (They didn't have a bye week this season with their former teams, and the Jaguars already had theirs, so the team is choosing to rest them this week.) The defensive tackle position should be okay with Godchaux getting added to the rotation, but at safety, Rayuan Lane III will have to hold up as a secondary starter for one more week. Can the Navy man add another takeaway to his resume before Bates replaces him? Henry : The X-Factor on Sunday will be Quinn Ewers. How many passes can Ewers end up throwing if the real Jacksonville offense plays well? Do we live in a world where Cam Ward plays the whole game, and Ewers plays garbage time in the late third or fourth quarters, yet they have comparable stats? I think we do. Final score prediction? Dillon : Jaguars 31, Titans 17 Travis : Jaguars 38, Titans 17 Gus : Jaguars 30, Titans 13 Henry : Jaguars 35, Titans 6 What are your Week 10 predictions, Jaguars fans? Let us know in the comments! These newcomers join a team that already holds a three-game lead in its division. They will also line up on the other side of the ball from an offense that is cooking with gas. The fourth-highest-scoring unit in the NFL has flat-out demolished half of its opponents. Trevor Lawrence , somehow, is still somewhat flying under the radar — probably because his offense keeps building such large leads that he does not need to rack up passing numbers in the second halves of these blowouts. Parker Washington has turned into a star, and Bhayshul Tuten emerged as a bona fide No. 1 running back. All of the pieces are in place. Just when it seemed like the Patriots were starting to put everything back together, they hit another rough patch. Just like they did to open the season, they have lost two of their last three games. The only win in that stretch was a five-point squeaker against the lowly Miami Dolphins . The road ahead does not get a whole lot easier with five likely playoff teams on the schedule over the next eight weeks. It is going to be a battle to return to the postseason after last year's run to the Super Bowl. Don't look now, but the Houston Texans are not out of it yet. The AFC South will remain out of reach so long as the Jaguars do not shockingly collapse, so it is Wild Card or bust for a squad that started the year at 0-4. At just 1.5 games back, the Texans are right in the mix. Since that winless first month of the season, the Texans have won three of four and took two of those games in blowout fashion. They just put up a season-high 44 points on the bottom-dwelling Los Angeles Chargers in a game that emphasized how far C.J. Stroud has come as a quarterback. The Packers are the only team with three losses, so every matchup means a little bit more to them as they try to work their way out of the shallow basement of the NFL's best division — one that could send all four teams to the postseason . They will have vengeance on their minds on Sunday as they seek to get payback for what the Minnesota Vikings did to them in a stunning second-half comeback in Week 1. The Jacksonville Jaguars made not one, but two big splashes ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. Jacksonville first acquired one-time Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III in a trade with the Atlanta Falcons on Tuesday, before landing Super Bowl champion defensive tackle Jordan Davis in a move with the Philadelphia Eagles. The Jaguars also brought in defensive tackle Davon Godchaux before the deadline in a trade with the New Orleans Saints. Jacksonville head coach Liam Coen said on Friday that neither Bates nor Davis would be playing in the Jaguars' Week 10 road game on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans , but Godchaux will be suiting up. Coen explained that the decisions were based on whether each of the trio's old teams had already had their bye week or not. Bates played in each of Atlanta's first nine games this fall and hasn't missed a contest since the 2022 campaign, which was his final one with the Cincinnati Bengals. Davis, likewise, suited up in Philadelphia's first nine games this season and hasn't missed a contest since 2022, which was his rookie campaign. The 26-year-old University of Georgia product would've been taking his bye week with the rest of the Eagles right now anyway. Godchaux played in all of New Orleans' eight games this season and already had his bye during Week 8. Jacksonville had its bye in Week 7 and at 6-2, has a sizable lead in the AFC South. The second-place Houston Texans are 3-5. Coen may be thinking that the Jaguars can get away with resting Bates and Davis, as the Titans are just 1-7 and have the 28th-ranked offense in the NFL at 18.0 points per game. Jacksonville, meanwhile, enters Week 10 with the second-ranked defense at 15.1 points allowed per contest. Bates and Davis will get their first chance at making their Jaguars debuts in Week 11 when Coen and company travel to face the NFC East-leading New York Giants on Nov. 22. The pair of newcomers could then play their first home games in a Jacksonville uniform in Week 12 when the Jaguars and Titans square off again on Nov. 29.

home.headline: Jakobi Meyers Injury Update Takes Concerning Turn for Jaguars Before Week 10 vs. Titans
home.blurb: The Jacksonville Jaguars opened Week 10 practice without one of their top receivers. Jakobi Meyers did not practice Wednesday because of an ankle injury, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reported. Meyers was listed with hamstring and ankle injuries last week but played through them. He was on the field for 68 percent of the offensive snaps and caught four passes for 65 yards in the Jaguars' Thursday night win over the Baltimore Ravens. It isn't clear whether the ankle got worse or Wednesday was a maintenance day, but a missed practice is a step back from last week, when he was limited. Running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) and defensive end Travon Walker (rib) also did not practice Wednesday , and all three played through those injuries in Baltimore. Trade deadline additions Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out for rest. By our count, Meyers has caught 26 of his 37 targets, a 70.3 percent catch rate, for 374 yards and two touchdowns in eight games, according to ESPN . That works out to 14.4 yards per catch. His season high of 83 receiving yards came against the Houston Texans in London. He followed a two-catch, 24-yard game against the Indianapolis Colts with his 65 yards in Baltimore. picks.headline: The Colts and Dolphins Are Potentially Playing for the Number One Pick This Week, but Indianapolis Already Traded It Away
picks.blurb: The Colts and Dolphins Are Potentially Playing for the Number One Pick This Week, but Indianapolis Already Traded It Away - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football FAA ground stop updates Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Brian Marr · Men's Journal Fri, November 13, 2026 at 7:13 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When the Indianapolis Colts take the field against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, they will be a shell of the team that they were around this time last season. This time last year, the Colts looked like one of the best teams in the conference. They were just coming off a 31-25 overtime victory against the Atlanta Falcons in Germany and had recently acquired cornerback Sauce Gardner from the New York Jets. It would be Indianapolis's last win of the season. They lost starting quarterback Daniel Jones to an Achilles tear and lost their final seven games to finish 8-9. This season hasn't been great either, as they've started 2-7 with five straight losses heading into Sunday's game. All told, the Colts are just 2-14 since beating Atlanta last season and have been one of the worst teams in the league. This stretch of bad play made the Colts sellers at the deadline this season. They parted ways with starters such as DeForest Buckner and Keenan Allen, who went to San Francisco; Quenton Nelson, who was traded to Seattle; and Josh Downs, who is now in Kansas City. It is clear that they are fully in on a tank. The Miami Dolphins have also been upfront about tanking this season. This past offseason, they released Tyreek Hill and Tua Tagovailoa and traded Jaylen Waddle. Three of those players helped Miami make multiple playoff appearances. So Miami is struggling, as to be expected. To date, they have won only one game, a 28-25 victory over the New York Jets. They will also be starting Kyle McCord at quarterback after starter Malik Willis was placed on injured reserve. So what we have as these two teams kick off at 1 p.m. Eastern on Sunday: a good old-fashioned Tank Bowl. The winner gets bragging rights, and the loser gets a better draft pick. Or at least that is how it would usually work, but whether the Colts win or lose is irrelevant to the chase for the first overall pick. Going back to that trade for Sauce Gardner last season, the Colts gave the Jets two first-round draft picks. One in 2026 and the other in the upcoming 2027 draft. So Colts fans can safely root for what's left of their team this weekend, while New York Jets fans will find themselves in a strange position, rooting for their rivals in the Miami Dolphins.

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Miami Dolphins (1-7) and Indianapolis Colts (2-7) meet Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium in a matchup between two teams racing towards the top of the 2027 Draft. The Dolphins have lost two straight and sit in the cellar in the AFC East while the Colts have lost five in a row and have only the Titans between them and a spot in the basement in the AFC South. The headline as these teams take the field is that Miami’s starting signal-caller, Malik Willis , has been placed on the IR and as a result, rookie Kyle McCord will get the first start of his career. Indianapolis will continue with Daniel Jones , who has 1,722 passing yards and six touchdowns this season. Jones, however, has struggled to regain the form he had prior to tearing his Achilles late last season. Miami’s latest setback was a 19-9 home loss to the Detroit Lions, a game in which the Dolphins’ defense did enough to give the offense a chance but Miami never reached the end zone. Willis completed just 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards with an interception, while Ollie Gordon II led the Dolphins with 55 rushing yards and Caleb Douglas caught six passes for 70 yards. Miami finished with only 228 total yards, went 0-for-3 in the red zone and settled for three Zane Gonzalez field goals. Indianapolis’ last loss was considerably more painful. The Colts rallied from a 17-7 halftime deficit against Dallas, getting a 55-yard touchdown catch from Ashton Dulin and field goals of 59 and 50 yards from Spencer Shrader to take a 23-20 lead with 1:37 remaining. But Dak Prescott immediately hit Ryan Flournoy for 46 yards, and Javonte Williams scored from a yard out with 1:08 left to give Dallas a 27-23 victory. Jones finished 20-of-34 for 180 yards, a touchdown and an interception, while Jonathan Taylor managed only 46 yards on 13 carries and lost a costly fourth-quarter fumble. Dallas piled up 508 yards to Indianapolis’ 271, illustrating the biggest concern for a Colts’ team that is allowing 361.8 yards and 27.7 points per game. The central storyline, then, is which struggling offense can take advantage of an accommodating opponent. Miami is averaging only 15.8 points per game, 31st in the league, and will be asking McCord to make his debut on the road; Indianapolis averages 20.4 points but carries a -11 turnover differential, making ball security especially important for Jones and Taylor. Recent history favors the Colts. Indianapolis has won the last three meetings, including a 33-8 rout at Lucas Oil Stadium in Week 1 of the 2025 season, when Jones completed 22 of 29 passes for 272 yards and a touchdown and Taylor rushed for 71 yards. The broader history belongs to the Dolphins, who hold a 48-30 advantage across 78 regular-season and postseason meetings. away.blurb: The only other player who has now been hit with a DNP (did not participate) is rookie wide receiver Chris Bell. Bell is still dealing with a knee injury, which is connected to his torn ACL that he suffered at the end of his collegiate career in 2025. Bell has appeared on the injury report off and on since returning in Week 1 to play, and now he was downgraded from a limited participant on Wednesday to DNP on Thursday. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee ), edge Malik Herring (neck), tight end Will Kacmarek (quad/knee), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) were all limited. Some good news in these listed players is that Kacmarek was upgraded to limited after missing Thursday's practice. Baker also remains limited, which could mean that he is not yet ready to play. The cornerback has made his return to practice after not playing in 2026 due to suffering a knee injury in training camp. There is still a chance that Baker could play, but the usual case is that players who remain limited likely need a week or so more to fully get back to being able to take the field. Wright has been dealing with a quad injury that led to him being ruled out in Week 9. Now, he is set to return against the Colts. away.headline: Breaking Down the Good News/Bad News Regarding Dolphins WR Chris Bell
away.blurb: Head coach Jeff Hafley said that Bell likely would be listed as doubtful for the game at Lucas Oil Stadium because of a knee injury, but the good news here is that it's not related to the torn ACL that Bell sustained last November during his final season at Louisville. Instead, Bell was injured in practice Wednesday when he took a hit to the knee. He wound up being listed as limited for that day, didn't practice Thursday and Hafley he also wasn't going to practice Friday. The only other player that Hafley said would be out is wide receiver Jared Wayne, who sustained a quad injury in practice Thursday. His absence should mean a return to the lineup for veteran wide receiver Jalen Tolbert, who's had a pretty forgettable season after signing with the Dolphins as a free agent in the spring. Lastly, Hafley repeated what he had said before about rookie linebacker Trey Moore, who remains on IR with a pretty significant ankle injury he sustained in the preseason opener at Washington. Hafley said he was "hopeful" that Moore would be able to return at some point this season, though that time doesn't appear imminent and it's probably 50-50 that he'll be back at all in 2026. Veteran Jalen Tolbert's Return to the Sidelines Highlights Dolphins Week 9 Inactive List Breaking Down the Good News/Bad News Regarding Dolphins WR Chris Bell Skip to main content SI.COM Rookie wide receiver Chris Bell likely won't play for the Miami Dolphins against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10, but the update on his status actually wasn't terrible news in the big picture. It's a setback of sorts, for sure, for the rookie third-round pick, but anytime we see Bell and knee on the injury report, there's reason for concern. It's overall been a tough rookie season for Bell, though he did surpass a lot of expectations by being ready for the start of the regular season. The production, however, has been very pedestrian. Bell has appeared in all eight games this season, but he's got only 12 catches for 148 yards for a 12.3-yard average with no touchdowns. Worse, he's been held without a catch three times, including during the 19-9 loss agianst the Detroit Lions last Sunday when he was targeted only once. On that pass attempt, Bell failed to get separation on a slant, an issue that's popped up regularly this season. Some of that, of course, could be attributed to Bell still working his way back after the knee injury. The hope, of course, is that Bell can finish with a flurry this season to possibly carry some momentum heading into 2027 because he did flash high-end potential in college. Bell's status was just one of the injury updates that Hafley provided Friday when he also indicated, as expected, that center Aaron Brewer will miss the Colts game because he's still in concussion protocol. Hafley confirmed that Andrew Meyer will take his place at center in the starting lineup. Tight end Will Kacmarek should be ready to go after missing practice Wednesday with quad and knee issues.

away.headline: First Injury Report of Week 10: Dolphins Offense Could Be Even More Short-Handed Against Indianapolis
away.blurb: The Dolphins released their first injury report of Week 10 on Wednesday and what stood out was center Aaron Brewer not practice because of a concussion. While it's too early to rule out Brewer for the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium, the fact he didn't practice Wednesday doesn't bode well. Based on the Return to Play protocol for players dealing with concussions, it's probably a must that Brewer practice Thursday on a limited basis for him to have a chance to play against the Colts. Robinson had to sit out the Week 2 game against San Francisco, while Proctor missed the Week 8 game against the New England Patriots. It should be noted that ahead of that New England game, cornerback JuJu Brents also missed the Wednesday practice because of a concussion before he was limited Thursday and a full participant Friday. He ended up playing against the Patriots. The other issue to monitor on offense involves rookie wide receiver Chris Bell, who is back on the injury report with limited participation in practice because of a knee issue. First Injury Report of Week 10: Dolphins Offense Could Be Even More Short-Handed Against Indianapolis Skip to main content SI.COM Quarterback Kyle McCord is set to make his NFL debut for the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, but it might have to do without having the team's All-Pro center snapping him the ball. And rest assured the Dolphins will be very careful not to rush him into action. The Dolphins unfortunately are becoming accustomed to having to deal with concussions, as both edge defender Chop Robinson and guard Kadyn Proctor missed a game this season because of that issue. Brewer played every snap against the Lions during the 19-9 loss Sunday, so this llikely was another case of him reporting symptoms the following day. The other player on the 53-man roster who didn't practice Wednesday was rookie tight end Will Kacmarek, who is dealing with quad/knee issues. He left the game against Detroit after taking a big shot to the side of the leg after a short reception and was seen at practice Wednesday wearing a compression sleeve on his left leg. If he were unable to play against Indianapolis, it likely would mean more reps for fellow rookie Seydou Traore, who's gotten more involved on offense is recent weeks and also would mean an appearance by waiver wire pick-up Justin Joly. Bell, who is nearing the one-year anniversary of the torn ACL he sustained in his final season at Louisville, last was on the injury report before the Week 5 game against the Cincinnati Bengals. It's logical to think, though not certain, he's dealing with some soreness in his surgically repaired knee. That obviously isn't a great development after he wasn't on the injury report at all for the past three games. Bell played 36 offensive snaps against Detroit after playing 45 against the New England Patriots. He was targeted only once against the Lions, the result being an incomplete pass. Published Nov 11, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Alain Pou

home.blurb: Wide receiver Chris Bell has been limited in practice this week with a knee issue. Hafley said he would not practice on Friday and is doubtful, but he has not been ruled out. Hafley said Bell got hit in the leg during practice and it did not have to do with his prior knee injury. Hafley said he expects Chop Robinson and Josh Uche to step up in defensive lineman Zach Sieler's absence . Sieler is out for the season after season-ending biceps surgery. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts Miami Dolphins All-Pro center Aaron Brewer remains in concussion protocol and will not play against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. Hafley also said his new quarterback has a "very calm confidence" about him. "He's got a quiet leadership about him. He's got a confidence to him. He's very calm in the huddle. And he seems to be grasping everything really well," Hafley said. "I think he's done a really good job in the two practices that we've had. (Friday's) a big day again, getting more in the red zone and polishing up some stuff. "But again, this will be a process, right? I'm not going to expect him to look perfect. There's going to be hopefully some really good moments for him and then there's going to be some that we're going to have to continue to grow in these next games. But I'm excited for him and I appreciate how he's worked, attacked the game plan and how he's kind of communicating and developing chemistry with the players around him in the huddle." "The way Chop's playing and really practicing, I think he's a great example of what it's supposed to look like," Hafley said. "And I think he's going to grow into one of those roles."

picks.blurb: Saints Rookie Report: Week 10 preview vs. the Panthers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football FAA ground stop updates Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Saints Rookie Report: Week 10 preview vs. the Panthers NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 08: Jordyn Tyson #0 of the New Orleans Saints avoids a tackle Ronnie Hickman #33 of the Cleveland Browns during a game at Caesars Superdome on November 08, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Caleb Yaccarino · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A big game is right around the corner for the New Orleans Saints, and hopefully, after the trade deadline, the rookies can lead the Saints to a win. WR Jordyn Tyson It was an exciting debut for Tyson. Yes, he fumbled on his first catch, but it was a really great play by the Browns defender, and Tyson will learn not to reach like that if he is not close enough to the end zone. But after that, when he was able to play, Tyson was open every time he was on the field and picked up some very important yards. Per head coach Kellen Moore, Tyson will have a larger role in the offense in Week 10, and he could have an incredible performance against the Panthers. DT Christen Miller I really do not know what to say anymore. Miller was a healthy scratch on Sunday. I wish there was more clarity on this situation because it makes zero sense why he is not playing. Miller has been a whelming run defender and has made little impact in pass rush, which is perfectly fine. He needs to play more. Hopefully, after the Davon Godchaux trade, Miller can have more snaps, even if he's not the starter. TE Oscar Delp I hoped that Delp would be more involved in the offense, but that didn't happen. Maybe if he were the receiver instead of Noah Fant on that drop, the Saints would have scored a touchdown on that play. The Saints need to start prioritizing the youth on this roster, and I'm hoping Delp can finally get some consistent targets against the Panthers. OG Jeremiah Wright News on Cesar Ruiz's injury has not been released yet, so it's unknown if Wright is going play, but if he does, good luck to him. The Browns defensive line is very good, and it's going to be his biggest test yet. He wasn't horrible against the Steelers, but it was also not good, and he looked like a rookie out there. That's the expectation, but the Saints will need to see more from him against the Browns. WR Bryce Lance It's time for Lance to be benched and not involved in the offense. He was thrown to once and dropped the ball, which completely stalled the drive and was outperformed by his fellow rookie WRs. Lance is a good blocker, but he's making consistent mistakes. WR Barion Brown Now to Brown; he had a much better day. Like with Tyson, Brown made a really bad mistake that resulted in a fumble, but outside of that, he had a great day. Brown was getting the Saints in great field position on nearly every return and had a 50+ yard catch in this game. I'm hoping that Brown can take over Lance's snaps and potentially get a few catches against the Panthers. RB CJ Donaldson Donaldson has been injured and is lower on the depth chart now. OT Mason Murphy It seems like Kelvin Banks Jr. is on his way back, so Murphy's chances of starting become even lower. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. As usual, Styles will likely stick with the special teams unit, but it will be interesting to see what happens if Justin Reid gets traded.

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Carolina Panthers (3-5) and the New Orleans Saints (3-5) have each struggled mightily at times this season and yet they meet Sunday in the Bayou improbably tied atop the NFC South despite each having lost five of their eight games. Carolina has lost three straight after falling 26-21 to Denver, while New Orleans has won two of its last three and is coming off a 23-22 overtime victory over Cleveland. Carolina’s skid reached three games last Sunday against the Broncos, 26-21. A bright spot was the improved play of Bryce Young who completed 28 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Chuba Hubbard carried the ball 16 times for 79 yards and Darren Waller caught eight passes for 90 yards. Carolina finished with 353 total yards and averaged 4.8 yards per rushing attempt but couldn’t turn that production into a win. The Panthers statistical profile underlines their issues. They average 24.9 points and 362.4 yards per game, including 261.1 through the air, but Carolina surrenders roughly 27 points per game. New Orleans comes in with considerably more momentum after surviving last Sunday in Cleveland, knocking off the Browns 23-22 in overtime. QB Tyler Shough helped erase a fourth-quarter deficit and then directed a 74-yard touchdown drive to open overtime, finishing it with a 15-yard touchdown pass to Juwan Johnson . The New Orleans defense generated five sacks, with Carl Granderson getting two. The win was the Saints’ first home win of the season. This rivalry has been remarkably competitive historically, although New Orleans has controlled it recently. The Saints swept Carolina last season and now lead the all-time series 34-29, including their lone postseason matchup. Their most recent meeting came last season on December 14, in New Orleans, when the Saints upset the Panthers 20-17 on Charlie Smyth’s 47-yard field goal with two seconds remaining. away.headline: Panthers admit unusual mistake involving injured RB Jonathon Brooks
away.blurb: The Panthers opened Brooks’ 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve on Wednesday, and he was listed as a full participant for Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practice sessions. Brooks, as well as cornerback Mike Jackson, took scout team reps and should have been listed as limited for both of those days. Both Brooks and Jackson were officially listed as doubtful for Sunday’s Week 10 matchup against the New Orleans Saints. Starting running back Chuba Hubbard has stepped up in a big way with Brooks unavailable. Through eight games this season, he has 619 rushing yards, five rushing touchdowns, 167 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns — serving as the engine of the Panthers’ offense. Related Articles NFL Insider Explains Ravens’ Lamar Jackson Return Window Carolina Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks was placed on injured reserve after sustaining groin and core muscle injuries in Week 2 of the 2026 season, causing him to miss each of the last six games. But on Friday, a Panthers team spokesperson admitted those designations were a mistake. The Panthers’ running back depth chart is thin behind Hubbard, featuring Trevor Etienne, AJ Dillon and Anthony Tyus III. Carolina is 3-5 to begin their 2026 campaign, dropping each of their last three games. However, they still sit atop the NFC South standings — tied with the Saints. Sunday’s Week 10 clash against New Orleans will kick off at 1 p.m. ET. away.headline: Struggling Panthers could get 5 starters, 4 reserves back from injuries in the coming weeks
away.blurb: Carolina opened the 21-day practice windows on Wednesday for cornerback Mike Jackson, wide receiver Xavier Legette and running back Jonathon Brooks to return from injured reserve. Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips, guard Damien Lewis and cornerback Will Lee III returned to practice after missing time with injuries, while versatile offensive lineman Brady Christensen entered his second week in the 21-day practice window and is nearing his return. Coach Dave Canales said it's too early in the week to know who'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Saints. The Panthers held a light practice on Wednesday, and Canales said he should know more later in the week once the medical staff is able to evaluate the injured players' progress. away.headline: Panthers rookie's return in new defensive scheme comes at a critical time with tough matchup waiting against the Saints
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The good news for the Panthers is that the team is getting healthier at the right time. Multiple reinforcements from the IR were back at practice , and could be back on Sunday, and star outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips is ramping back up for a return as well. However, the most critical return going into this game for the Panthers could be rookie cornerback Will Lee III, who missed last week’s game with a hamstring injury. “It felt good just to be back in my comfort zone,” Lee said, via Joe Person . “Just being back to what I was doing in college for all those years. It’s real fun to have it, I’m excited to get back out there.” So, this is going to be a matchup quarterback Tyler Shough is going to be looking at if the Panthers show man. And it’ll be on Lee, along with whoever starts opposite him, to lock down these two wide receivers on Sunday. We’ll see if “The Blanket” is up for that one-on-one challenge and if this scheme can help get the best out of his game. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Back in college, Lee was at his best as a press-man corner and that physicality on the outside is a big reason why the Panthers were attracted to him in the draft. Yet, during his first seven games, Lee had 141 coverage snaps in zone compared to 41 coverage snaps in man. Last week against the Denver Broncos, the team’s two outside cornerbacks played 46 coverage snaps in man and 26 coverage snaps in zone. That change is going to be very beneficial for Lee once he’s back in action, and something he’s already appreciated getting back to in practice. home.headline: Panthers’ Jaelan Phillips gets concerning injury downgrade before Saints game
home.blurb: The Carolina Panthers ' defensive blueprint for their Week 11 matchup against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday could require adjustments following the latest update on outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips . After participating fully in Wednesday's practice, the pass rusher was downgraded to limited on Thursday's injury report because of his lingering hamstring issue. Although Phillips' full participation on Wednesday appeared encouraging, that session was only a walk-through, making Thursday's limited designation a more telling development. Phillips was not the only starter whose practice status changed Thursday. Left guard Damien Lewis (knee) also went from full participation to limited, while linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) was the only player who did not practice. Cornerback Will Lee III (hamstring), who missed last week's game, returned to full participation, as did starting cornerback Mike Jackson (groin). The Panthers will be hoping Phillips can return soon, given the difference his pass-rushing production could make to their defense. He initially suffered the problem in Week 4 versus the Detroit Lions before aggravating it during his first game back against the Philadelphia Eagles following the bye week. Carolina has since taken a cautious approach with the defensive playmaker. His absence has affected the Panthers' ability to generate pressure. Phillips recorded 2.5 sacks and six quarterback hits across his first five appearances. However, Carolina managed just one sack and four quarterback hits throughout his three-game absence. Patrick Jones II accounted for the team's only sack against the Denver Broncos last week. home.headline: Panthers Week 10 injury report: Offense gets a big return vs. Saints
home.blurb: Panthers Week 10 injury report: Offense gets a big return vs. Saints - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Panthers Week 10 injury report: Offense gets a big return vs. Saints Wide receiver Xavier Legette (knee), offensive lineman Brady Christensen (hamstring), outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) and cornerback Will Lee (hamstring) III are all considered questionable for Sunday's matchup against the Saints . Legette, Christensen and Phillips practiced in full in Friday while Lee was considered limited. Carolina will likely be without running back Jonathon Brooks (groin) and cornerback Mike Jackson (groin)—both of whom are down as doubtful. In addition, linebacker Bobby Okereke has been ruled out due to his foot injury. On the bright side, the Panthers will get a big return in left guard Damien Lewis—who was sidelined from the past two games with a knee issue. The Jets are now 2-7 on the season. All playoff hopes have evaporated. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-21 record. We are reaching Kotite-ish levels of ineptitude. This week the Jets visited the Kansas City Chiefs. They kept it competitve for a half. In the first half the Jets outgained the Chiefs. They won the turnover battle. They had more than twice the time of possession as the Chiefs. They scored on four out of five possessions. The Chiefs scored only twice. And still the Jets trailed at halftime, 14 – 12. It was an ill omen. The second half was all Chiefs. They scored 21 unanswered points and cruised to a 35 – 12 blowout over the Jets. It was just one more humiliation in a decade filled with them. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-7 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets limp home to face the first place Buffalo Bills in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Bills have won three straight games and six of seven on the year. Josh Allen is playing like an MVP candidate, as usual. The Bills offense is humming, leading the NFL in points scored. The Bills defense has had some issues, but they held the Baltimore Ravens to 144 yards of offense and just 10 points last week. This will be a formidable challenge for a reeling Jets team just trying to stop the bleeding. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Bills will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets home underdogs by 8.5 points. The game has an over/under of 51.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Bills are -520. Any given Sunday and all that jazz, but an upset here seems like a bridge too far for the Jets. Perhaps they can keep the game competitive for a while as they did against the Chiefs for a half. picks.headline: Pick Six: Buffalo Bills at New York Jets
picks.blurb: Pick Six: Buffalo Bills at New York Jets - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football FAA ground stop updates Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Pick Six: Buffalo Bills at New York Jets ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - JANUARY 04: Running back Ray Davis #22 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball during the fourth quarter against the New York Jets at Highmark Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. The Bills defeated the Jets 35-8. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bent Double · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Jets will be a home underdog against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, having lost seven of their last eight games. Other than a last-gasp loss to the Patriots in week four, the Bills' record is unblemished this year. Surely the Jets can't pull off an upset, can they? Here are six storylines to watch as New York seeks to flip their season on its head: It's a trap! America is already looking ahead to the Bills-Chiefs game scheduled to take place in the evening of Thanksgiving Thursday. While Buffalo has two games to play between now and then, they will feel good about their chances of still only having one loss after playing the Jets this week and Miami next week. Kansas City has lost just twice so this could be decisive in the race for the AFC's top seed. We've seen situations like this before though. While the Jets are rarely the team to take advantage of the opportunity, their profile as a team that has kept a lot of games close and come up just short in the end could make them dangerous if the Bills get complacent. And if they did get complacent, who could blame them? After all, the last time these teams met, the Bills rested all of their starters and still won 35-8. Then again, that was a very different Jets team too. The only current non-offensive line starters who started that game are Harrison Phillips, Jamien Sherwood and Adonai Mitchell. Can Mitchell bounce back? It's become traditional this year to have at least one high profile player that doesn't get the ball on offense. Last week, it was Adonai Mitchell, a player who seven days earlier, had posted the best numbers of his career. The Jets really seem to be struggling with the whole "many mouths to feed" aspect of having provided their quarterback with an adequate number of pass catching weapons for the first time in several seasons. However, Mitchell not seeing the ball last week was not for the want of trying as he was thrown to seven times. Opening drive success We could easily spend column inches here talking about why the Jets can't convert in the red zone, or how they shouldn't abandon the running game, or when are they ever going to intercept another pass, but how about we discuss something they have actually been doing well? For each of the past five games, the Jets have driven downfield and scored on their opening possession, which has played a big part in them still being competitive heading into the second half of each game. So, now we have to ask the question – can this continue? And…how will the team react if it doesn't? This isn't the first time in recent memory that the offensive has looked good early on in games, and executed the scripted part of the gameplan effectively, only to then go on to struggle in the second half when points are needed to convert wins. Back in 2020, where Adam Gase's Jets were in danger of going winless until very late in the season, they actually scored eight times in a row on their opening drive. The current decision makers would ideally not like to have too many similarities to that 2020 team. Gregory Rousseau's ascent to super-stardom The biggest threat on the Bills defense is obviously edge rusher Gregory Rousseau, who is having a monster year. After just eight games, Rousseau has already tied his career-high with eight sacks, while also doubling his career mark for passes defensed with another eight. Rousseau primarily lines up on the left, so it will be mostly up to Armand Membou to try and keep him quiet. Rousseau had a two sack game against the Jets in his second season in 2022, but surprisingly otherwise only has one sack in eight other games against the Jets. The Bills are 7-2 in these matchups, though. Having not been traded, is Will McDonald's role going to change? The Jets opted not to trade former first round pick Will McDonald during the week, despite reports of interest from a number of teams. Head coach Aaron Glenn has been suggesting McDonald is still very much in the Jets plans for the rest of this season, and he is of course under contract for next year after New York exercised his fifth year option. He even implied McDonald had earned a bigger role. McDonald's defensive snap count percentage has dropped from 66% in both 2024 and 2025 to just 46% in 2026 and, even more confoundingly, his percentage of run snaps has increased. Will an increase in playing time for McDonald happen on Sunday? And, if it does, are we destined to see diminishing returns in regard to his production? What's the plan for the secondary? A matchup against the team with the number one offense in the entire NFL is not really the ideal time to experiment with line-up changes but the Jets are desperately striving for more consistency from their back seven, in addition to having an undermanned front that is struggling to stop the run. Having missed a meeting and made some on-field mistakes, the previous starting slot corner – Jarvis Brownlee Jr. – is in the doghouse. However, rookie D'Angelo Ponds has looked overmatched at times which is hardly surprising given how he is learning a new position and missed half of training camp. New York also experimented with using Minkah Fitzpatrick in the slot on Sunday, elevating Malachi Moore into the lineup at safety for basically the first time all year. Could this be the answer? Time will tell. Let us know how you see things going in Sunday's game in the comments section…
