Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Buffalo Bills (7-1) visit the New York Jets (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium, with the AFC East rivals heading in dramatically different directions. Buffalo sits three games clear of second-place New England atop the division while the Jets have lost four in a row and sit but a half-game out of the cellar in the AFC East. The Bills enter the week with the NFL’s highest-scoring offense at 32.0 points per game and lead the league with 386.4 yards per game, powered by Josh Allen and a rushing attack featuring James Cook III . The Jets, meanwhile, are averaging just 20.2 points per game which begs the question: Can Geno Smith and the Jets score enough to keep up with the Bills’ elite attack? Working in the Jets’ favor is that Buffalo has a short turnaround after grinding out a 23-6 road victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. It was a far more physical game than the final score suggests. The Bills managed just three points on their first six possessions, and Allen threw an early interception, but his 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds remaining in the first half gave Buffalo a 10-6 advantage. From there the Bills wore down Minnesota, holding the ball for an extraordinary 42:32 and running 79 offensive plays. Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards, including a five-yard fourth-quarter touchdown, while Allen finished 21-of-31 for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Buffalo’s defense was even better, limiting Minnesota to 178 total yards and nine first downs while forcing three turnovers. The Jets return home after a 35-12 loss at Kansas City. Despite an early 6-0 lead, New York’s offensive woes were impossible to ignore. Smith and co. repeatedly stalled and had to settle for four Jason Sanders field goals. The Chiefs led just 14-12 at halftime before completely controlling the second half. New York finished with only 229 yards, went 2-for-12 on third down and failed to score a touchdown, while Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards and was sacked five times. Breece Hall returned from a five-game absence caused by a quadriceps injury and produced 87 yards from scrimmage, while rookie Omar Cooper Jr. led the Jets with eight catches for 58 yards. Recent history adds another challenge for New York. Buffalo has won eight of the past 10 meetings, including a couple smacks last season, beating the Jets 30-10 at MetLife Stadium on Sept. 14, 2025 and 35-8 in Buffalo on Jan. 4, 2026. picks.headline: Bills vs Jets prediction and key matchups for tricky division game
picks.blurb: News Sports Life Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals BILLS Bills vs Jets prediction and key matchups for tricky division game Sal Maiorana Rochester Democrat and Chronicle Updated Nov. 13, 2026, 1:47 p.m. ET ORCHARD PARK - If there was a moment when the team-wide frustration that the New York Jets have experienced this season boiled to a head, it was last Sunday in Kansas City when quarterback Geno Smith momentarily lost his mind. In the second quarter of what became their fourth straight loss, the Jets were leading 9-7 when Braelon Allen lost a fumble that was recovered by Chiefs safety Alohi Gilman. As Gilman began his return, Smith rushed over and launched himself with intent and knocked Gilman flat at the Jets 24, a stunning display of physicality from a quarterback. “It's something that you really don't want to happen, but competitors are going to compete, so I'm not surprised that it happened, but that's something that you don't want from your starting quarterback,” coach Aaron Glenn said. Smith knew the fumble was a huge mistake and sure enough, the Chiefs scored two plays later and grabbed a lead they never relinquished in their 35-12 blowout. Later in the game, following another failed Jets possession, Smith came to the sideline and slammed his helmet to the ground, the inevitability of falling to 2-7 clearly getting to him. As usual in mid-November, the Jets are already in playing-out-the-string mode, but they have a great chance to make a statement Sunday when they host the 7-1 Buffalo Bills . There isn’t too much left to play for downstate, but beating the AFC’s No. 1 team and damaging the Bills’ quest for the No. 1 seed would certainly provide some professional joy, especially considering the two 30-10 and 35-8 beatings Buffalo put on New York last year. “We're not going to hide from the fact that we're 2-7,” said Glenn, who is likely coaching for his job so every possible victory is crucial. “We own that, but man, we're still working our (butts) off to make sure we fix that. We like the players that we have in the building to be able to help us do that. When you look at the seven losses, and this is just the facts, five of the teams were playoff-caliber teams. I think five of them were one-score games. There's a number of things that we got to fix and get better at, but we feel like, man, we're right on the cusp of trying to break through.” Joe Brady claims he never pays attention to the standings or an opponent’s record, but he knows the Jets are 2-7, and he also knows that a few plays here or there could have altered the course of their season. He and his team won’t be taking a division opponent lightly. “This is a division game on the road, it's going to be as hard as it gets, right?” Brady said. “We’ve showed that we can go on the road and win a hard game (actually seven straight dating to 2025), we got to go do it again. (Glenn’s) going to have them ready to go as he should. We know we're always gonna get everybody's best as we should, and we're gonna have to bring it to be able to come out with a win. We know it's not gonna be easy, but we wouldn't want it any other way.” Here’s my preview of the game, followed by my prediction: The QB Matchup: Josh Allen vs. Geno Smith One of the reasons why Allen continues to be perhaps the best QB in the league is the way he has been able to adapt to whatever is required to win a game. Some weeks he has needed to throw the ball downfield and bite off big chunks, in others he needed to stay patient and work underneath. Some games he needed to use his legs to jump start the offense, in others he needed to lean on James Cook and the running game. “Everything starts with the quarterback,” Glenn said. “He's playing at a high level, which he always does, so we're looking forward to the competition.” Allen is tied for the league lead at 8.6 yards per attempt and is second in yards per completion at 13.0, yet his 99.3 passer rating is a smidge less than Smith who has been better than the Jets’ record would indicate. Smith’s 100.5 passer rating through nine weeks is the highest by a Jets quarterback at this point of a season since the 1970 merger. He’s completing 67.5% of his passes which ranks fifth in the league and his 1.1% interception rate is fourth-best, so this is not going to be Joe Fagnano or Carson Wentz that the Bills’ defense is facing. Buffalo Bills who should impact the game ▶ TE Dalton Kincaid: The best part of Kincaid’s season thus far is that he has played in every game, something that had been an issue for him the previous two seasons. He has 30 catches for 429 yards and two TDs, but again, you long for more. His 14.3 yards per catch is second-best among TEs behind only Travis Kelce (14.6), so Allen needs to start finding ways to get him the ball beyond the 38 targets he’s seen. ▶ C Connor McGovern: The Jets defense ranks 26th in the league allowing 128 rushing yards per game and has been gouged for 29 runs of at least 10 yards, tied for the fourth-most in the league. McGovern and the rest of the Bills’ line has paved the way for the second-best rushing attack fronted by Cook, and given the Jets’ 39.9% blitz rate, sixth-highest in the league per Next Gen Stats, the Bills would love to catch them with quick hitters through the A and B gaps. ▶ DT Ed Oliver: He started to knock some rust off against Minnesota and played his best game of the season. He had seven pressures and for the season, Sumer Sports has him charted for 109 pass rush snaps and his 19.3% pressure rate is No. 1 among interior linemen. And though he’s only had 45 run snaps, he has been very effective with a 15.6% run stop percentage which is second-best. But Oliver and the rest of the D-line has a big test against a solid Jets offensive line. ▶ CB Dee Alford: After a rough start to his Bills career, Alford played his best game in Minnesota and was part of the reason why Wentz was so awful. But this will be a bigger test as the Jets have been using impressive WR Omar Cooper in the slot on about half his snaps and Cooper has been one of the best players in this rookie class. Alford will also find himself against the two Jets TEs who have excelled thus far, Mason Taylor and rookie matchup nightmare Kenyon Sadiq. New York Jets who should impact the game ▶ RB Braelon Allen: He pounced on an opportunity while No. 1 RB Breece Hall was sidelined for five weeks and in those games, Allen averaged 101 yards rushing, 5.4 yards per attempt, and caught 13 passes for 70 yards. Hall returned last week against the Chiefs and ran for 68 yards despite playing 10 fewer snaps than Allen, and that seems to be an indication that the Jets will use both players in a rotation and that gives them an opportunity to play ball control and keep the Bills’ offense off the field. ▶ WR Garrett Wilson: He leads the Jets with 43 catches for 527 yards and three TDs despite missing last week’s game with a concussion, but his numbers would be even better if Smith utilized him more. Wilson has had five games where he was targeted seven times or fewer and that’s not ideal for a player who has big-play ability. Part of this is because the Jets have two other WRs in Cooper and Adonai Mitchell, and TEs Sadiq and Taylor who have made nice contributions, but Wilson needs more targets and especially if Christian Benford doesn't play - he's questionable with a wrist injury - you can bet Wilson will get them. ▶ LB David Bailey: The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 draft looks like a star in the making already and he’s going to present problems off the edge. He has 7.5 sacks and 31 QB pressures which lead the team, his 20 stops (plays that caused a failure for the offense) are second to LB Jamien Sherwood, and his five forced fumbles are the main reason the Jets lead the league with 13 total. Bailey lines up almost exclusively to the offense’s right, so with RT Spencer Brown doubtful and almost certainly not play, it's probably going to be Tylan Grable getting another start. That's a problematic matchup given Bailey’s explosive speed, though Grable has held up pretty well when he's had to play. ▶ S Minkah Fitzpatrick: He has become a big-time rival for the Bills as he has faced them eight times during his time with the Steelers and his two stints with the Dolphins. Now he’s with the Jets and he’s still at the top of his game and is one reason why the Jets have played pretty good pass defense. He has allowed just six receptions on 12 targets, and his 33 snaps per reception allowed is fifth-best among all safeties. Sal’s prediction: Bills 30, Jets 20 It’s hard to get to a place where I can think the Jets can pull the upset. Of course, I felt the same way in 2022 when a 6-1 Bills team went to New Jersey and lost 20-17, and in 2023 when Aaron Rodgers got hurt on the fourth play of the game and the Bills still found a way to lose. Even in 2024, it was all the Bills could do to pull out a 23-20 victory on a late Tyler Bass field goal. My point is division games on the road are tough. Remember last year in Miami? The Bills will need to be on point against a New York team that has a lousy record, but has emerging talent on both sides of the ball, especially on offense. In the end, with the Bills’ offense functioning at such a high rate, I don’t think the red zone-challenged Jets can keep pace. picks.blurb: News Bergen Sports HS Sports Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals JETS NY Jets vs Bills predictions and expert picks for Week 10 game Albert Bainbridge IV Dave Rivera Brian Marron Mike Dougherty Bob Jordan Art Stapleton Chris Iseman NorthJersey.com Updated Nov. 11, 2026, 3:50 p.m. ET Unfortunately for the New York Jets , one thing is constant: new week, same result. It was more of the same for the Jets last Sunday as they were shut out in the second half in another blowout loss − a 35-12 defeat at the hands of Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. The Jets, on a four-game losing streak, welcome in the Buffalo Bills , who are 7-1 and currently the No. 1 seed in the AFC coming off Monday night's impressive 23-6 victory on the road over the Minnesota Vikings . Like most opponents, the Jets have failed to keep up with the Bills in recent meetings. Gang Green has dropped five straight games against Buffalo and have been outscored, 160-58, in the process. The Bills have averaged 32 points per game over that time and the Jets have been unable to score 21 or more points in any of those contests. It'll be another uphill battle for the Jets, who were swept by the Bills in 2026, with Buffalo winning by three or more scores both times last season. Our NFL prognosticators are: Art Stapleton ( Giants /NFL writer, NorthJersey.com), Bert Bainbridge (sports trending reporter/columnist, NorthJersey.com), Brian Marron (digital producer, NorthJersey.com), Chris Iseman (Rutgers writer, NorthJersey.com), Mike Dougherty (sports writer, lohud.com), Bob Jordan (sports editor, Asbury Park Press/APP.com) and Dave Rivera (sports editor, USA TODAY Northeast/NorthJersey.com). Jets vs Bills Week 10 staff predictions, staff standings Brian Marron: 8-1 Dave Rivera: 8-1 Bert Bainbridge: 7-2 Bob Jordan: 7-2 Art Stapleton: 6-2 Mike Dougherty: 6-3 Chris Iseman : 6-3 Can the Jets keep it close, or will it be yet another Bills blowout victory in this head-to-head matchup? Here's our staff predictions for Jets-Bills on Sunday at MetLife Stadium: Bert Bainbridge The pick: Bills 34, Jets 20 Here's why: Even with the Bills coming off a short week after playing on Monday night, it doesn't matter here as Buffalo effortlessly puts up 30-plus points yet again versus a Jets defense that routinely is unable to get off the field or keep teams out of the end zone. The Bills win this one by only two scores as the Jets' losing streak reaches five games in yet another lost season. Art Stapleton The pick: Bills 37, Jets 20 Here’s why: The Bills are the best team in football and after a lackluster showing in spot of the prime time victory over Minnesota expect Josh Allen and this underrated defense to make another statement. The pick: Bills 30, Jets 16 Here's why: Too much Josh Allen, as the Bills pull away in the third quarter and coast to victory. For the Jets, this will have the same feel as last week's loss to the Chiefs. The pick: Bills 37, Jets 24 Here's why: This game doesn't require any meticulous analysis. Josh Allen and James Cook should have no issues shredding maybe the NFL's worst defense at the moment. The Jets should be able to score some garbage points to make the final score look better, but expect the Bills to cruise here. Mike Dougherty The pick: Bills 38, Jets 20 Here's why: Did you see how good the Bills defense looked in Minnesota? If the Jets are within a touchdown at halftime, it's a moral victory. away.blurb: Starting right tackle Spencer Brown was the only Bills player who did not practice Thursday because of an ankle injury. Brown was listed as a limited participant during Wednesday's walkthrough, when practice participation was estimated. The Bills have four starting offensive linemen on their injury report, including left tackle Dion Dawkins (rib), left guard Alec Anderson (ankle) and center Connor McGovern (neck). The Raiders have one of the worst defenses in the NFL, particularly when it comes to stopping the run. Meanwhile, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is preparing for his first NFL start against a Seattle defense that has been one of the toughest units in the league. I expect the Seahawks to take advantage of both matchups. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 4: Jadarian Price scores his first NFL touchdown Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images This could finally be the game when Jadarian Price gets into the end zone for the first time in his NFL career. It's been a challenging rookie season for the first-round pick, who has yet to find his footing in Seattle's backfield. However, this matchup could be exactly what he needs to change the trajectory of his season. The Raiders have struggled mightily against opposing running backs, and Price should have opportunities to make an impact. With Zach Charbonnet also back in the backfield, Seattle has more options to attack Las Vegas. It is expected Price will take advantage of his opportunities and finally get that first NFL touchdown. Bold Prediction No. 3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba records 10+ catches, 125+ yards, and at least one TD Even though Seattle should have plenty of success running the football, that doesn't mean Jaxon Smith-Njigba won't have a monster afternoon. JSN is coming off a relatively quiet performance against the Cardinals, finishing with seven catches for 51 yards without a touchdown. That is not the kind of production we've grown accustomed to seeing from one of the NFL's best wide receivers. I expect a much different performance against Las Vegas. The Raiders have struggled to contain opposing offenses. I think he gets back to dominating opposing secondaries. Bold Prediction No. 2: Seahawks' rushing attack finally has a monster game The Raiders are allowing a league-leading 151.2 rushing yards per game. That's an invitation for Seattle to establish its ground game and take advantage of one of the NFL's worst run defenses. Seattle averages 110 yards on the ground. The Seahawks have yet to consistently get their rushing attack going, but this is the perfect opportunity to change that. With rookie Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back from injury, Seattle has the personnel to make life miserable for Las Vegas. It shouldn't matter who is getting the carries. I expect the Seahawks to pound the rock throughout the afternoon and finish with close to 200 rushing yards. And remember, I still expect Smith-Njigba to have a monster game through the air. Seattle could realistically finish with more than 450 total yards of offense if everything goes according to plan. Bold Prediction No. 1: Fernando Mendoza has a nightmare game in his first NFL start Welcome to the NFL, Fernando Mendoza . The rookie quarterback is getting his first opportunity to lead the Raiders after the organization made a major change at the position. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings . Unfortunately, his first start comes against a Seahawks defense that can make life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Mendoza does have some talented tight ends to work with, but Las Vegas' receiving corps is underwhelming. Seattle should be able to make things uncomfortable for the rookie, particularly if its pass rush can consistently generate pressure. It wouldn't be surprising if Mendoza throws a touchdown pass at some point. However, I expect the Raiders' offense to struggle for most of the afternoon. The prediction is that Mendoza finishes with fewer than 175 passing yards and completes less than 65% of his attempts. His first NFL start will be a difficult learning experience, and Seattle's defense will be the biggest reason why. away.headline: Week 10 Injury Report: Seahawks at Raiders
away.blurb: The Seahawks will be getting a couple of players back from injury for Sunday's game in Las Vegas, with outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu and receiver Rashid Shaheed both ready to return after missing the past two games with ankle and knee injuries, respectively. The Seahawks will still be without four players who also missed last week's game: left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), quarterback Sam Darnold (ribs/quadriceps), guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger), all of whom were ruled out on Friday's injury report. Cross, who was able to practice Thursday on a limited basis, should be able to make it back after Seattle's Week 11 bye, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. Quarterback Drew Lock was limited all week due to elbow and oblique injuries, as was expected coming into the week, but he has no injury designation, and the plan is still for him to make his second straight start in place of Darnold. Defensive tackle Jarran Reed , who did not practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a personal matter, was back at practice Friday and will play, Macdonald said, clarifying that it was a good personal matter. For the Raiders, defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and receiver Dont'e Thornton (back), are listed as questionable. Thursday's report featured only a couple of changes for the Seahawks, including a significant one for the offensive line, with left tackle Charles Cross , who has missed the past two games with an ankle injury, listed as limited after not practicing Wednesday. The only other changes were that tight end AJ Barner , who was a full participant Wednesday with a finger injury, has been removed from the injury report altogether, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who got a rest day on Wednesday, was a full participant. As expected, quarterback Drew Lock was limited again, as has been the plan as he prepares to start while dealing with elbow and oblique injuries. Receiver Rashid Shaheed , who is trying to make his way back from a knee injury that kept him out of two games, was a full participant for the second day in a row, while Uchenna Nwosu , who is trying to get back from an ankle injury, was limited for the second day in a row. home.blurb: Sam Darnold has already been ruled out, so he won't play. Drew Lock was expected to be limited all week, but is expected to play in Week 10. Leonard Williams is already trending toward missing another game. He will be missed. Seahawks' Mike Macdonald rules Sam Darnold out for Week 9 vs. Cardinals The Seattle Seahawks are 5-4 and head to Las Vegas to play the 4-5 Raiders at Allegiant Stadium in Week 10. Seattle will be playing with a backup quarterback, Drew Lock, and Las Vegas will have a rookie quarterback, Fernando Mendoza, in his first career start. Head coach Mike Macdonald's team still has the better roster, and should be expected to win, but the Raiders are better this season than in quite some time. A victory against Seattle would be huge for their collective confidence. Health could be a factor. Seattle's injury report was fairly lengthy, so even some players who perform in Week 10 might not be close to 100 percent. At least, the bye week follows in Week 11. Seattle Seahawks injury updates for Week 10 Seattle will announce its full list of inactives an hour and a half before kickoff, and this article will be updated with the latest information. Raiders inactives and injury updates The Raiders are fairly healthy, but what doesn't show on their injury report is the trade of quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings. This means rookie Fernando Mendoza will start for the first time in the NFL. As with Seattle, Vegas will announce its inactives an hour and a half before kickoff. How to watch Seahawks vs. Raiders in Week 10 TV Network: CBS (KIRO 7 in Seattle) Announcers: Ian Eagle (play-by-play), Ross Tucker (analysis), and Evan Washburn (sideline reporter) In the Seattle area, you can also stream the game on NFL+, while nationally, you might need a subscription to YouTube TV's NFL Sunday Ticket to stream or watch the game. You can listen to the game on the Seahawks Mobile App, SiriusXM channels 123 or 269, Seattle Sports 710 AM, and KIRO Newsradio 97.3. Steve Raible will provide the play-by-play for the Seahawks broadcast, while Dave Wyman will do the analysis, and Jen Mueller will report from the sidelines. Storylines to watch for Seahawks in Week 10 Obviously, what most national fans will be interested in is how well the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft will do in his first career start . While Vegas trading Kirk Cousins made sense, Mendoza's first two starts couldn't come against tougher defenses: The Seahawks and then the Denver Broncos. Presumably, head coach Klint Kubiak isn't going to let Mendoza throw the ball 50 times, but he could have a somewhat conservative game plan to operate with. Kubiak is a good coach, so fans should expect a difficult challenge, even against a rookie quarterback. Will Drew Lock succeed against a non-Arizona Cardinals team? The difference between Lock games and Sam Darnold games has been significant this season. Lock has turned the ball over in three games. Darnold has nine interceptions in six games.

Whoever is under center will once again be working with a patchwork offensive line as stars Quenton Nelson and Charles Cross did not practice. Nelson is battling a knee injury that might hold him out for his second straight game while Cross has been out with an ankle injury since Week 7. Backup guard Anthony Bradford continues to be hampered by a knee injury and was limited on Wednesday. On the defensive side, Leonard Williams remains out with a stinger that he suffered against the Kansas City Chiefs, and edge rusher Derick Hall was limited with a new back injury. Both would be a massive loss for the Seahawks front that will hope to ruin Raiders' rookie Fernando Mendoza's debut. It wasn't all negative for the Seahawks' defense, though, as signs are trending positive for edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu, who was limited with the ankle injury that's held him out of the team's last two games. A Duel in the Desert: Los Angeles Rams vs. Arizona Cardinals Preview Los Angeles has dealt with injuries to several star players throughout the season, but last week brought their worst injury yet. Puka Nacua sustained a blow to his knee on the Rams' final offensive play, which left him with sprains to his posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) ,medial collateral ligament (MCL), and a case of turf toe. Now, Los Angeles must survive until Nacua returns. Head coach Sean McVay knows the Rams have what it takes to beat the Cardinals in their second matchup. "One of the calling cards for our group, and is always an expectation, is we play with passion and energy, and I think we would all agree that (the first game against the Cardinals) wasn't quite up to our standards," McVay said . Los Angeles will likely rely on running 13 personnel while several of their best receivers are sidelined with injuries. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford must spread the targets in order to keep Arizona's defense off guard. "It's not difficult to pull the trigger, I trust those guys," Stafford said . Nov 8, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) throws the ball against the Washington Commanders during the third quarter at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images While several receivers are injured, the Rams could also become a more defensively minded team. Los Angeles defensive coordinator Chris Shula has done a great job this year. He knows the defense will need to perform even better than it did when the Rams first played the Cardinals. "We didn't get the win so obviously it wasn't good enough," Shula said . Last time these two teams faced each other, the Rams' defensive unit held the Cardinals to six field goals. Last week, Los Angeles welcomed back Myles Garrett after his time on the injured reserve. He finished the game with three sacks, including a strip sack showing his dominance in a Los Angeles jersey for the first time. Garrett's Week 1 performance left much to be desired, especially since he was playing hurt. His return helped Los Angeles defeat the Washington Commanders 20-13. The team is also hoping to get top cornerback Trent McDuffie back from injury. Los Angeles desperately need McDuffie back if they want to keep their season alive. He has missed the past two games after injuring his back in Week 8. This season, McDuffie has been ranked as the third-best cornerback with an 89.8 rating according to Pro Football Focus (PFF). His pass coverage has been exceptional, and he has lived up to expectations in the first year of his massive $124 million deal . Los Angeles is also without their other top cornerback Jaylen Watson , who is out for the season after undergoing shoulder surgery a few weeks ago. Other cornerbacks Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes Jr. have stepped up in his absence, but McDuffie's services are still needed. The Last Word Los Angeles' season could already be over with the number of injuries to key players, but regardless of who's available to play, the Rams must keep pushing for the playoffs. The team is currently riding a three-game winning streak since their loss to the Cardinals. Now, they will have another chance to defeat the Cardinals and former Rams offensive coordinator , Mike LaFleur. The key to this weekend is play-calling. If McVay can keep the Cardinals' defense off balance and use everyone in the pass game, the Rams will be in a strong position to win. Like McVay, Stafford must also be at his best. Coming off an MVP season, Stafford is the glue that must hold the offense together while his best targets are sidelined with injuries. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The favorites in August to claim the Lombardi Trophy, the LA Rams (5-4) currently sit on the wrong side of the playoff bubble as they prepare to take on the Arizona Cardinals (3-6) Sunday in Glendale. The Rams’ struggles are the result of injuries and consistently inconsistent play. That said, they take the field riding a three-game winning streak that has pushed them into a tie with Seatle for second in the NFC West. The Cardinals are last in the division as a result of losses two of the last three weeks. Los Angeles has climbed back into the playoff chase behind Matthew Stafford , who has thrown for 2,374 yards and 16 touchdowns. Arizona averages only 19.8 points per game while surrendering 28.3, but there is one significant reason the Rams won’t take the Cardinals lightly: Arizona already beat them 18-16 on Oct. 18 at SoFi Stadium. Los Angeles extended its winning streak to three last Sunday with a 20-13 road victory over the Washington Commanders. The Rams’ defense has been central to the turnaround, holding the Chargers to nine points and Washington to 13 in consecutive weeks, and Los Angeles enters Sunday allowing only 20.1 points and 312.9 yards per game. The major concern is what Stafford will have around him. Star receiver Puka Nacua , the team’s leading receiver with 715 yards, is out after suffering knee and toe injuries, while Davante Adams remains on injured reserve with a hamstring injury and tight end Terrance Ferguson is also sidelined. It is up to Head Coach Sean McVay and Stafford to keep the offense functioning even with several of its most important weapons sidelined. Arizona’s most recent outing was far less encouraging. The Cardinals followed up a thrilling and improbable 33-30 overtime win in Dallas with a 17-3 loss at Seattle. The Cardinals are now 3-6 and, remarkably, 0-3 at home, while an offense already struggling for consistency is undergoing a major change at quarterback. With Gardner Minshew placed on injured reserve, rookie Carson Beck is set to make his first appearance against the Rams, putting even more importance on running back Tyler Allgeier and tight end Trey McBride , who leads Arizona with 598 receiving yards and five touchdown catches. The recent history makes this matchup particularly interesting because as noted earlier, Arizona has already pulled off one of the season’s bigger divisional upsets. On Oct. 18, the Cardinals went into SoFi Stadium and beat the Rams 18-16 despite failing to score a touchdown, riding six field goals from Chad Ryland . Los Angeles took a 16-15 lead with 46 seconds remaining on a Stafford touchdown pass to Colby Parkinson , only for Arizona to drive back into field-goal range and win on Ryland’s 43-yarder as time expired. That result interrupted what had otherwise been a Rams-dominated stretch in the rivalry: Los Angeles beat Arizona 45-17 in December 2025 and 37-20 in January 2026, and the Rams lead the complete series 53-42-2, including a 2-0 postseason record. away.blurb: Los Angeles’ newly traded edge defender, Myles Garrett, has been out since Week 2 after arthroscopic surgery in mid-September. He has no injury designation for the Week 9 matchup against the Washington Commanders on Nov. 8. The Texas A&M alum practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday and Thursday but not Friday. The Washington alum suffered a back injury while making a tackle during a Week 8 game victory over the Los Angeles Chargers. The 26-year-old cornerback did not practice all week. He is still listed as questionable for Week 9. He may be a game-time decision - probably depending on how he feels this Saturday, Nov. 7. The re-aggravation of his right shoulder dislocation ended his 2026 season. He did not practice all week. He is listed as out for Week 9. ​The 2025 draft pick was expected to be activated from injured reserve this Saturday, Nov. 7, and return to the lineup. But a brand new hamstring injury has complicated the matter. Rams wide receiver Davante Adams has been out for several weeks with a hamstring injury; if Ferguson had joined the lineup for Los Angeles quarterback Matthew Stafford in Week 9 vs. Washington, it would have helped. But the Oregon product is listed as out in the final Los Angeles Rams injury report. Grant Stuard and Kam Curl are questionable, Joe Cardona is doubtful Kam Curl suffered a foot injury, likely sustained during the Rams’ Week 8 win over the Chargers, as per RotoWire. The safety did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, but he participated in a limited capacity Friday. He is listed as questionable for the Week 9 game vs. Washington. Long snapper Joe Cardona did not practice all week due to an ankle injury he suffered in Week 7 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders. He did not play in the Week 8 vs. Chargers. home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: Report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start. home.headline: Cardinals Forced to Sign 40-Year-Old QB as Injuries Mount
home.blurb: “I think probably even stronger than how I said it yesterday. I wasn’t anticipating some of the things that we found out today. I knew that particularly on offense — (with) the defense there’s been a guy here and there, but there’s been some decent continuity over the last month, and I think you guys see that," LaFleur said. Cardinals Coach Said The Quiet Part Out Loud on Carson Beck ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals' Monday has taken a steep twist thanks to several significant injuries to their offense, and with news of Gardner Minshew potentially being done for the season, the organization has already targeted their next passer. From ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter: "With veteran QB Gardner Minshew sidelined due to a UCL injury, the Cardinals are signing QB Josh Johnson off the Bengals’ practice squad, per sources. The Cardinals will be Johnson’s 15th NFL team in 14 NFL seasons." Johnson, a perennial backup veteran quarterback, will be the team's No. 2 quarterback as the Cardinals prepare for their Week 10 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams — who just welcomed Myles Garrett back to the mix with a three-sack performance this Sunday. Minshew was injured on the final play of the second quarter against Seattle. He returned to finish the game but showed obvious discomfort. Rookie quarterback Carson Beck is slated to start for Arizona this week. Johnson, 40 years old, first entered the league as a fifth-round pick in the 2008 NFL Draft. He's played 50 NFL games with 11 starts, most recently starting twice for the Washington Commanders in 2025. In those two games, Johnson completed 34 of 54 passes for 372 yards for one touchdown and two interceptions. He has a 2-9 record as a starter. It was an extremely tough day for the Cardinals, who lost both Minshew and Michael Wilson . Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur says the team has to regroup, even amid the injuries. "I think you see 11 has won more and more each week, particularly over these last four weeks. Not the case on offense right now and that’s what I meant by that. There’s been a lot of moving parts, and I have to do a better job of stabilizing that to make sure that we don’t have performances like we did yesterday.” The Cardinals recently dealt Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens last week, thinning their quarterback room down to two. With Minshew injured, Beck was the only healthy quarterback on the roster prior to Johnson's signing. picks.blurb: Expert predictions for Cowboys-49ers: Can Dallas climb to .500 with a huge upset? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football FAA ground stop updates Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) throws an incomplete pass to wide receiver Michael Gallup as he's pressured by San Francisco 49ers defensive end Drake Jackson (95) during the first quarter at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California, October 8, 2023. (Tom Fox/Dallas Morning News) SportsDay Staff · Dallas Morning News Fri, November 13, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Will the Cowboys finally be able to climb back to .500 and pick up their first marquee win of the season? They'll have a massive opportunity to do just that Sunday when the San Francisco 49ers come to AT&T Stadium as the two teams renew their historic rivalry . Dallas enters the game with a 4-5 record and, after the Commanders' win over the Giants on Thursday, a chance to climb even with New York in the win column. Meanwhile, San Francisco enters the game with a 7-1 record and has quickly established itself as one of the NFL's Super Bowl favorites. Can the Cowboys pull off an upset and get their season back on track? The Dallas Morning News ' columnists and beat writers gave their predictions below. Tim Cowlishaw The good news for Dallas is the 49ers can't really take advantage of the Cowboys' challenged secondary because of their injury troubles at wide receiver. The bad news is the 49ers can take advantage of everything else. A team that plays with grit despite its current 7-1 record, San Francisco figures to dominate time of possession with its multi-pronged running attack, and it will take some huge plays from Dak Prescott against the league's No. 3 defense to keep the Cowboys engaged for long in this one. The recipe is there for a Cowboys loss. The Cowboys haven't pieced together back-to-back wins in nearly a year, despite many opportunities along the way. The 49ers might be the class of the NFC, with an offense that continues to score, despite a ton of injuries, and a defense that is as fast as it is physical. Will this be the week the Cowboys finally stack two wins in a row? It's unlikely. 49ers 35, Cowboys 28 You won't find many (any?) realistic NFL fans giving the Cowboys a shot to win this week. Any path to victory would include the 49ers making self-inflicted mistakes and Dallas' offense playing flawlessly. Yes, the Cowboys' offense performs much better at AT&T Stadium, but it still disappears for long stretches during games. Even Brandon Aubrey has struggled to find his range of late. The red-clad fans will have plenty to cheer for in Arlington. Abraham Nudelstejer Given what we've seen this season, this is probably the easiest prediction to make so far. The Cowboys already have lost at home to a team whose season is all but over, and to another that could still reach the playoffs only because of the woeful state of its division. There is no tangible evidence of improvement that would justify picking Dallas to beat a squad that, with just one loss all year, appears destined to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl. The best Dallas can realistically hope for is to put up a spirited fight and begin preparing for next week's game. 49ers 34, Cowboys 13 Kevin Sherrington Jerry Jones did the right thing by not mortgaging any more of his future to try to save this season, and this game against the 49ers should do nothing but affirm that decision. The Cowboys won't hang 500 yards on the 49ers like they did the Colts. San Francisco has the third-best defense in the NFL, meaning Dak Prescott can't hope to outscore them. 49ers 31, Cowboys 24 Calvin Watkins If the postseason started today, the 49ers would be the No. 1 seed. The Cowboys? Well, you know what's happening with them. If the Cowboys want to get back into the playoff chase, and that's winning the NFC East, beating the 49ers is a good start. It's a difficult task considering how good the 49ers are on defense (ranked third in total defense) so the Cowboys' offense will have to be near-perfect. That's hard to do. The 49ers should handle things. 49ers 30, Cowboys 17 This article originally published at Expert predictions for Cowboys-49ers: Can Dallas climb to .500 with a huge upset? .

away.headline: Mike Evans ruled out, Trent Williams questionable as NFC-leading 49ers' injury concerns persist
away.blurb: The San Francisco 49ers will be without wide receiver Mike Evans for a third straight game Sunday after ruling him out against the Dallas Cowboys as he continues to deal with Achilles tendinitis. Evans and Williams were not the only concerns for San Francisco this week. Coach Kyle Shanahan said cornerbacks Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green were also on the injury report. Both missed practice Wednesday and Thursday after suffering injuries in last week’s game against Las Vegas, but they were limited participants Friday. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw was also listed as questionable after hurting his knee at practice Thursday, while cornerback Nate Hobbs (adductor), defensive back Upton Stout (shoulder, neck) and defensive tackle C.J. West (knee) were also questionable. "The left tackle in general is always huge. Then a guy of Trent’s caliber is huge," Shanahan said. "Just the way he plays out there, down in and down out, what he means to the team, just his presence, the type of person he is, and just what he brings on game day. He’s a captain for a reason, and everyone knows Trent Williams is one of the best players in this league." San Francisco will have more help at receiver this week with Deebo Samuel set to return after missing the past three games with a hamstring injury and Keenan Allen set to make his debut for the 49ers after being acquired earlier this week in a trade from Indianapolis. Original article source: Mike Evans ruled out, Trent Williams questionable as NFC-leading 49ers' injury concerns persist Meanwhile, it remains unclear whether standout left tackle Trent Williams will suit up after injuring his shoulder in practice this week. Injuries are an unavoidable part of the NFL , but few teams have dealt with them as consistently as the San Francisco 49ers have in recent seasons. Their injury report has become a weekly storyline. At 38, Williams remains a 12-time Pro Bowler playing at a high level, making his availability significant for San Francisco. He left practice early Thursday and did not participate Friday, but Shanahan remained hopeful the veteran tackle would feel well enough to play Sunday. Vederian Lowe would likely start if Williams is unable to go, but replacing the longtime standout would be a major challenge for the 49ers. But they will be missing Evans again after he left a Week 6 game against Washington early with the injury. He missed the next two games and has been unable to practice since then but is making progress. Shanahan said there’s a chance Evans could play next week in Mexico against Minnesota. The 49ers enter Sunday’s game with an NFC-best 7-1 record. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

away.headline: NFL executive has concerning prediction for 49ers’ Christian McCaffrey
away.blurb: McCaffrey carries no game designation for Sunday’s matchup with the Dallas Cowboys. He sat out Wednesday for rest, then practiced fully Thursday and Friday. Related Articles What George Pickens’ Bizarre Answer Means for His Cowboys Return vs. 49ers Texans Hit With Major Injury Blow as 4 Key Starters Ruled Out Against Browns San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey has scored 10 touchdowns through eight games, helping his team build a 7-1 record. One NFL executive still expects the 49ers to need more from rookie running back Kaelon Black before the season ends. The executive’s praise for Black came with a prediction about McCaffrey getting injured. “He’s an explosive runner,” an NFC executive told ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler of Black, adding that “Christian [McCaffrey] will undoubtedly get hurt at some point.” Fowler included the comment in a Friday report on the NFL’s playoff races and emerging players. The executive was not identified and did not offer a reason for the injury prediction. The 30-year-old has appeared in all eight of San Francisco’s games this season. He leads the team with 457 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns, adding 36 catches for 270 yards and another score. Only tight end George Kittle has more receptions for the 49ers. Kaelon Black earns work alongside Christian McCaffrey Black has already become a regular part of coach Kyle Shanahan’s offense. He has 68 carries for 303 yards and a touchdown, averaging 4.5 yards per attempt. His 133 rushing yards over the past two games include a 30-yard touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons. In last Sunday’s 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, Black carried 11 times for 70 yards. McCaffrey had 18 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown, along with two catches for 19 yards and another score. That gave San Francisco 138 rushing yards from its top two backs, with Black accounting for more than a third of their combined carries. The rookie also handled double-digit rushing attempts in the season opener against the Los Angeles Rams, finishing with 65 yards on 14 carries. McCaffrey’s workload remains below last season’s pace. He finished the 2025 regular season with 311 carries and 102 receptions across 17 starts, totaling 2,126 yards from scrimmage and 17 touchdowns. He won the AP Comeback Player of the Year award. Through eight games this year, McCaffrey has 138 touches for 727 yards from scrimmage. His receiving role remains far larger than Black’s, who has three catches for four yards. McCaffrey caught nine passes against Washington and six against Atlanta before San Francisco’s bye. He has scored at least one touchdown in seven straight games, including two-touchdown performances against Miami, Washington and Las Vegas. home.blurb: Mike Evans 'Real Close' to a Return? "Mike's such a dog and wants to get out there all the time. And I think it'd be hard to keep him out if this was the last game or anything like that," Shanahan explained . "But what we're trying not to do is have him come back and then be out right away. We're trying to build him up the right way, so hopefully, it can last a little bit." NFL Network's Mike Garafolo said on Nov. 8 that Evans was "questionable at best" for the Cowboys game. He also compared the injury to the Achilles tendinitis that sidelined Christian McCaffrey two seasons ago. That's a big bounce back for a player who was limited to eight games in his final season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers because of a hamstring injury and a broken collarbone. He finished that year with 30 catches, 368 yards and three touchdowns. The 49ers have split their two games without him. They lost for the first time this season to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7. Then they came out of the bye and beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 on the strength of five second-half takeaways. Second-year wideout Jordan Watkins made one of the plays of that game with a leaping 37-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, all with Deebo Samuel also out. Samuel was limited in practice this week with a hamstring injury. That means Brock Purdy could be missing both of his top receivers again when the 49ers take on a Cowboys defense that has given up 236 points in nine games . home.headline: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan Gives Injury Updates on 2 Players Ahead of Cowboys Game
home.blurb: Two of those injuries are in the secondary. Renardo Green sustained a back/shoulder injury during the 49ers' Week 9 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, while Deommodore Lenoir is dealing with a lingering shoulder/neck issue that has forced him to practice in very limited capacities over the last few weeks. The 49ers also have rookie cornerback Ephesians Prysock and could potentially activate Nate Hobbs, who's been on injured reserve all season. Hobbs has had his practice window open to return and has fully participated in practice this week. 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan Gives Injury Updates on 2 Players Ahead of Cowboys Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan Gives Injury Updates on 2 Players Ahead of Cowboys Game SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers looks on during the second quarter against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty Cole Sullivan · HEAVY Fri, November 13, 2026 at 3:24 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The San Francisco 49ers are dealing with a string of injuries entering their Week 10 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. That said, neither player has practiced so far this week. After both showed up as DNPs on Thursday, their availability for Sunday is in serious doubt. Kyle Shanahan Gives Update on Green & Lenoir Appearing weekly on KNBR, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked whether Green and Lenoir could still play if they didn't practice Friday. That's usually the day when teams get a better idea of whether a player will be ready to go. Shanahan revealed that neither player has to practice Friday, even though he'd like them to, to remain in consideration as a possible active for Sunday's game. "They don't have to," Shanahan said. "Of course I would like to. But they've been here long enough and I trust them long enough to talk to them Saturday and Sunday and see where they're at." If both Green and Lenoir can't go, it would certainly make things a bit more complex for Raheem Morris' defense in the secondary. That said, San Francisco still has some trusted options. The team re-signed veteran cornerback Jack Jones to the practice squad this week, and it could activate him to the 53-man roster to play meaningful snaps. Safety Upton Stout wore a non-contact blue jersey during Thursday's practice, but he's been operating that way for weeks now. Barring a change, he should be able to suit up Sunday. home.headline: 49ers Have Added Two New Players to Their Injury Report for Sunday’s Game vs. Cowboys
home.blurb: On Friday, the San Francisco 49ers released their injury report for this Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys, per Nick Wagoner of ESPN. It isn't much of a surprise that wide receiver Mike Evans will be out of action again due to a case of Achilles tendinitis that kept him out of their previous two games. In addition, the Niners' defense is banged up. Starting cornerbacks Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir are listed as questionable with foot and back injuries, respectively, while safety Upton Stout is questionable with shoulder and neck ailments. Left tackle Trent Williams and off-ball linebacker Dre Greenlaw were limited participants in practice on Thursday because of shoulder and knee injuries, respectively. Both men are listed as questionable for Sunday's contest. The good news for San Francisco on the injury front is that wide receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. will make his return from a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 5 versus the Seattle Seahawks. His presence is badly needed with Evans and wideouts Christian Kirk (meniscus) and De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) still out of action. Kyle Shanahan Gives Hopeful Update on When Mike Evans Could Return for the 49ers 49ers Have Added Two New Players to Their Injury Report for Sunday’s Game vs. Cowboys - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Robert Marvi · Athlon Sports Sat, November 14, 2026 at 2:28 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads But two new players have been added to the team's injury report, which means that San Francisco could be seriously short-handed versus the Cowboys. Williams continues to play outstanding football at age 38. Pro Football Focus (subscription required) has given him grades of 81 in run-blocking, 87.6 in pass-blocking and 87.7 overall so far this season, and he ranks eighth, second and second, respectively, among offensive tackles in those three categories. Greenlaw, meanwhile, is having a great year himself. Nearly three years removed from tearing his Achilles, he is looking about as spry as ever with 57 total tackles (27 solo) and three tackles for loss on the season. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said that if Greenlaw isn't able to play, rookie Jaden Dugger will take Greenlaw's place at Will linebacker. Dugger, a fifth-round draft pick, has started three of eight games this year and posted 36 total tackles (25 solo), two tackles for loss, one QB hit, one sack and one pass defended. Sunday will also mark the Niners debut of veteran WR Keenan Allen, whom they acquired in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts on Tuesday. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense. … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) (SNF) Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. Pittsburgh always seems to be right in the thick of it in these division games, and the first matchup was decided by only three points. I think the scoring margin is the same here, but with slightly lower scoring, in keeping with the trend of divisional rematches. … Prediction: Bengals 23, Steelers 20 Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) (MNF) Dajani ( Chargers +4.5): This is potentially the worst Monday night game of all time. A winless team that hasn't covered the spread since last year vs. a spiraling team starting a new quarterback. Jacoby Brissett is an upgrade over Joe Fagnano , but how much of an upgrade immediately? I don't have a great read on this matchup, but I'll take Jim Harbaugh to keep things close with his brother's old team. … Prediction: Ravens 20, Chargers 17 Dubin (Chargers +4.5): I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. LA's offense is pretty broken, but the Ravens haven't exactly been great defensively (25th in scoring defense), so the Chargers might be able to put at least some points on the board. … Prediction: Ravens 24, Chargers 20 Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Da

picks.headline: Steelers vs Bengals Same Game Parlay: Best SGP Picks
picks.blurb: Pickswise - Expert Sports Picks & Predictions NFL NCAAF NBA NHL NCAAB UFC More Sports News Betting Casino Playzone Get App Bonuses Home Steelers vs Bengals Same Game Parlay: Best SGP Picks Table of Contents Bengals ML (-180) Over 49.5 (-108) Tee Higgins Over 75.5 receiving yards (-110) and to score a touchdown (+120) Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season continues with Sunday Night Football between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. It is huge matchup in the AFC North, where everyone is still in contention. These two teams are currently tied at the top with twin 6-2 records. Here is my SGP for Sunday’s primetime festivities, which get underway at 8:20 pm ET on NBC. Also be sure to check out our full Steelers vs Bengals predictions . Bengals ML (-180) Over 49.5 (-108) Tee Higgins Over 75.5 receiving yards (-110) Tee Higgins to score a touchdown (+120) Parlay odds: +625 Part of the value in a Same Game Parlay, of course, is that all of its components can be correlated if you so choose. That is the entire plan here, as Cincinnati receiver Tee Higgins having a big night would obviously work well with a win by the Bengals and plenty of points being scored. Let’s break down each of the three legs. Pittsburgh prevailed 30-27 in the first head-to-head showdown on September 27, but I’m not too concerned. The Steelers have swept the Bengals in a regular-season series only once since 2019. Aaron Rodgers’ squad overachieved in the first half of this season, but the first nine weeks were hardly convincing. Cincinnati, on the other hand, was mightily impressive en route to its six victories. Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are looking unstoppable. Even the defense has become an average unit – and average means good by the Bengals’ standards on that side of the ball. I’m not willing to give more than a field goal in this AFC North rivalry matchup (or really in any game involving two teams from this division), but the Bengals should be able to win it outright. This correlates nicely with the Bengals on the money line. After all, you can be almost certain that a whole bunch of points will be scored if the game is played at Cincinnati’s pace. Pittsburgh, of course, would much rather play more of a defensive slog. The first meeting between these two teams in 2026 resulted in 57 points, obviously an encouraging sign for another over on Sunday. The Bengals have not slowed down, either. In fact, they have only been getting better and better. Burrow and company have put 31, 35, 43 and 34 points on the board in their last four outings. Although Cincy’s defense has stepped up in recent weeks, keep in mind that this is a unit that got torched for 36 points by the lowly Titans earlier this month. The Bengals also watched the Steelers churn out 7.0 yards per play in this season’s first head-to-head matchup. Cincinnati ranks dead last in the entire NFL in opponents’ yards per rush (5.0), so Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren can be expected to go borderline crazy in this one. He turned 17 attempts into 127 yards against Cincy earlier this year. Tee Higgins Over 75.5 receiving yards (-110) and to score a touchdown (+120) Higgins has been on a heater of late – and really this entire season. The Clemson product has caught 48 of 67 targets for 758 yards and six touchdowns. He has produced at least 148 yards in three of the last five games and has scored five touchdowns in the past three weeks. Yes – five touchdowns in the past three weeks. Burrow is playing like an MVP candidate (if not even the favorite) and Chase always demands a ton of attention from opposing defenses. Elite cornerback Jamel Dean will likely be on Chase for the most part, which means things could open up for Higgins. When these two teams faced each other back in Week 3, Higgins made six receptions on seven targets for 90 yards and one TD. picks.headline: Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final
picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football FAA ground stop updates Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final (Sam Greene/The Enquirer / USA TODAY) Keegan Nickoson · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 11, 2026 at 11:53 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Joe Burrow accounts for four touchdowns for the fifth straight game Burrow is on a heater, scoring four or more touchdowns, whether throwing or running, in four straight games. In his last four games against the Steelers, Burrow has thrown 11 touchdowns and four interceptions, topping 275 yards in all four games. Interestingly, Pittsburgh is a great matchup for Burrow. The Steelers play zone coverage on 84.3% of dropbacks, according to Next Gen Stats, and Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL against zone by completion percentage, at 74.7%. Jaylen Warren rushes for 120-plus yards Warren has become one of the league's most productive running backs this season, ranking sixth in rushing yards and first in yards per carry, at 5.9. Earlier this season against the Bengals , Warren ran for the second-most yards of his season, with 127. Two weeks ago against Cleveland, Warren topped that number with 143 yards. It was the first time all season he rushed for 100 yards in back-to-back games. The Bengals' defense has been inconsistent this season, struggling with tackling some weeks and shutting down opposing offenses and forcing takeaways in others. I think that, coming off a bye, the Steelers catch the Bengals on their back foot and feed Warren, who will have a big game. Steelers win 34-31 History is not on the Bengals' side in this matchup. After playing an overseas game, teams are 0-5 when their next game comes against a team coming off a bye. The Steelers are rested, while the Bengals are recovering from nearly a full week in Madrid. A lot is at stake in this game, with the winner taking sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Pittsburgh doesn't have much momentum, especially on offense, as its best wide receiver, DK Metcalf, has been struggling with drops lately. He has just 378 receiving yards this season and has topped 100 yards just once, with a 115-yard day against Cleveland earlier this season. Metcalf had just one catch for 4 yards on six targets against the Browns. The Steelers hit a snag at the right time, giving themselves a week to figure things out. I think the Steelers pick up a big win, halting the Bengals' momentum and getting a massive tiebreaker. Pittsburgh has done a relatively good job of keeping a cap on Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins over the last couple of seasons. Outside of Chase's massive 16-catch, 161-yard game with Joe Flacco at quarterback last season, neither has topped 100 yards in their last four meetings.

picks.headline: Bengals vs. Steelers Final Score Predictions: Experts predict if the AFC North switches leaders on Sunday night
picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers Final Score Predictions: Experts predict if the AFC North switches leaders on Sunday night - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football FAA ground stop updates Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Brandon Little, John Sheeran, Rob Gregson · AtoZ Sports Fri, November 13, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) and Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) are getting set for a primetime bout for the AFC North lead on Sunday night. Our AFC North beat writers all see this game going in one direction. Bengals 33, Steelers 27 Neither the Bengals nor the Steelers made a trade deadline move despite being at the top of the division, and that was a surprise to me. The Steelers have the benefit of coming off a bye here, while the Bengals are fresh off an overseas win. The Steelers took the first matchup 30-27, but I don't see the Bengals dropping two games to these guys during the regular season. Cincinnati has much more firepower, but it's going to be all about what the defense can do at home in Week 10. Pittsburgh found real success both through the air and on the ground back in Week 3. Specifically, Jaylen Warren had himself a day that the Bengals can't allow to happen again. I think Cincinnati gets the home win here, but it'll be close, just like we all expect. Pittsburgh not adding wide receiver help doesn't look great when you consider what Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins can do on the other side. Joe Burrow goes for a big game, and the MVP talks get louder coming out of this one. – Brandon Little, A to Z Cleveland Bengals 27, Steelers 24 The second meeting between the Steelers and Bengals this year will be one of the biggest in recent memory. Whoever wins this game will be in the driver's seat for an AFC North Championship. The first match was tight, and a couple of special teams blunders allowed the Steelers to capitalize late and get the victory. If Pittsburgh wants any chance of replicating that success, it cannot allow Burrow to start 14/14 passing again and finish with a 75 percent completion percentage. Patrick Graham must change the picture this go-round. The Cincinnati Bengals have a 94% chance to make the NFL playoffs and an 8% chance to win Super Bowl LXI, according to the A to Z Sports NFL Playoff Predictor (updated Tue, Nov 10). Teams are 0-5 when coming off an international game and facing a team coming off a bye. The Steelers are rested and could be getting multiple starters, including star Derrick Harmon back from injury. But this Bengals team is humming. The offense under Burrow and with the weapons on the perimeter is among the best we have seen. They are going to hit the pressure points on the Steelers' defense (corners) and get the job done in a close-fought home victory. – Rob Gregson, A to Z Pittsburgh Bengals 31, Steelers 29 It's probably stupid to predict nearly the same score but reversed, but this is the outcome that makes the most sense to me. Cincinnati can do no wrong passing the football right now, and it doesn't look like something scheme can contain. Not when Burrow is telepathically connecting with Chase and Higgins week in and week out. They posted 27 points in the last meeting, and that's when they missed out on two possessions due to special teams mistakes. I think they break 30 this time. Cincinnati's defense isn't a ms trustworthy and that's how the Steelers can easily win. Warren and tight end Darnell Washington are the two biggest X-factors. If they each dominate a Bengals defense that struggles against elusive tailbacks in space, and has PTSD facing Washington (and good TEs in general), this has all the makings of a high-scoring rivalry game. Pittsburgh does have the rest advantage, but Cincy is the home team hosting an AFC North primetime game. The latter is typically the safer bet, so I'm going with it. – John Sheeran, A to Z Cincinnati Final Prediction for Bengals at Steelers The beat writers are all in agreement over the Bengals getting revenge and control of the division. The winner of the game will have the inside track to hosting a playoff game. Expect the best from both sides. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports.
