picks.headline: ‘Bring your popcorn’- Mike Tomlin makes bold prediction for Steelers-Bengals clash
picks.blurb: ‘Bring your popcorn’- Mike Tomlin makes bold prediction for Steelers-Bengals clash - Yahoo Sports Search query for Search Search News Finance More Mail NFL Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images Aryan Chadha · HITC Mon, 9 November 2026 at 11:30 am UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Premier League Scottish Football Champions League Europa League Club World Cup About our ads Mike Tomlin is expecting a blockbuster AFC North showdown between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals, backing both teams to deliver an entertaining contest with the division lead at stake. The former Steelers head coach knows exactly what this rivalry means after spending 19 years in Pittsburgh before stepping away from the role. He will now get to watch his old team from the NBC crew as the two sides prepare to meet on Sunday Night Football. Both teams enter the contest with 6-2 records and four consecutive victories, setting up a major meeting between two sides looking to strengthen their position in the AFC North. Mike Tomlin backs Steelers pass rush to challenge Joe Burrow and Cincinnati Bengals Tomlin made no secret of his excitement when discussing the matchup, admitting he would be more than happy to make the trip to Cincinnati. "It's AFC North football and you know I love that. You can airmail me right to Cincinnati," Tomlin said. He also highlighted the individual battle that could define the game, with Joe Burrow and the Bengals passing attack facing Pittsburgh's formidable pass rush. "It's good on good. Joe Burrow and that Cincinnati passing game vs T.J. Watt and the four-man rush of the Steelers…. Bring your popcorn and get your cameras ready." Pittsburgh will arrive with plenty of confidence after enjoying a bye week. The Steelers' four-game winning run includes a commanding 27-6 victory over the Cleveland Browns in their most recent outing. Cincinnati have also found their rhythm, beating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid. Burrow completed 82.8 per cent of his passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in that victory. However, the Bengals will have revenge on their minds after losing 30-27 to Pittsburgh during their earlier meeting this season. That defeat came during a difficult spell in which Cincinnati also suffered a second consecutive loss. Now, with both teams level at 6-2, the stakes are considerably higher. Tomlin will have a particularly interesting perspective from the NBC booth as he watches the Steelers take on a Bengals team that will be determined to settle the score on home turf. picks.headline: Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown
picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football FAA ground stop updates Cousins starting for Vikings Report: Jake Bauers to Red Sox Fantasy football lineup advice Poch to Man United Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown Alex Frank · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 12:05 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is as big of a home game as it gets for the Cincinnati Bengals . It's mid-November, against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and first place in the AFC North is on the line. Both the Bengals and Steelers are 6-2 and have both won four straight games. Not to mention, these two teams have already played this season. It was in Week 3, with the Steelers winning 30-27 in Pittsburgh. Right now on FanDuel , the Bengals are 3.5-point favorites next Sunday night. The Bengals' moneyline is -200, while the Steelers' is at +168. The over/under is at 47.5. Sunday night could be an extremely physical game. It's an AFC North rivalry with sole possession of first place in the division at stake. Also, it's the Bengals and Steelers. That's all you need to know for the potential level of physicality. Pittsburgh stole the first game against the Bengals, aided by two Bengals turnovers in the fourth quarter that included Joe Burrow getting strip-sacked with the Bengals on the edge of field goal range in the final minute. The Bengals never ran an offensive play with the lead in that game, but there were some great performances from their star players. Joe Burrow was 28/37 for 282 yards and three touchdowns, Ja'Marr Chase caught nine passes for 98 yards and a touchdown, and Tee Higgins hauled in six passes for 90 yards and a touchdown. Mike Gesicki also caught a 25-yard touchdown on 4th&2 early in the fourth quarter. For the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards and three touchdowns, while Jaylen Warren rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries. Eight different players caught a pass for the Steelers, with Darnell Washington leading the way with 67 receiving yards on three receptions. Roman Wilson, D.K. Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek each caught a touchdown for the Steelers. Rodgers currently has 1,871 passing yards and 13 touchdowns on the season, but he's also thrown six interceptions and is completing just 60.8 percent of his passes. Warren has 704 rushing yards and two touchdowns, while Washington and fellow tight end Pat Friermuth lead the Steelers with three and four touchdowns, respectively. T.J. Watt, as of Sunday night, leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks, and he also has nine tackles for loss. Cornerback Jamel Dean also has three forced fumbles. Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims held T.J. Watt off the stat sheet in that game, which bodes well going into Sunday night. The Bengals' offense scored on five of their eight drives in the first meeting in Week 3, gaining 352 yards of offense and rushing for 83 yards on 18 carries. Chase Brown rushed for 61 yards on 13 carries.

away.headline: Steelers vs Bengals: Injury update on DT Derrick Harmon
away.blurb: Harmon spoke to the media on Friday and hinted that he might be ready to roll on Sunday night, but said, "We'll see by tomorrow," meaning after the team's Saturday walkthrough. Our guess is that Harmon won't play this week but will be part of a larger group to return in Week 11 when the Steelers take on the Philadelphia Eagles , including wide receiver Roman Wilson. One of the most remarkable parts of the Pittsburgh Steelers success on defense this season is they have done it without defensive tackle Derrick Harmon. Harmon has been on the Reserve/Injured list and missed the last five games. But this week Harmon returned to practice as the team prepares to take on the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football, there is some hope he could be on the field. Fortunately, Monday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens could be one of their best chances to finally get into the win column. Baltimore is dealing with major injuries, including the absence of Lamar Jackson, and will turn to newly acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett . The Ravens are also struggling to find consistency at 4-5. Meanwhile, the Chargers are coming off another ugly loss after allowing C.J. Stroud to throw for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Could Jim Harbaugh finally get his team a victory? Here are three bold predictions for Chargers-Ravens on Monday Night Football. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 3: Jacoby Brissett throws for 2+ touchdowns in Ravens debut Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Brissett is now a Raven, and his first start with Baltimore will come at home against the Chargers . Los Angeles has a solid defense and typically does a good job making life difficult for opposing quarterbacks. However, that certainly wasn't the case against Houston. Stroud walked all over the Chargers on Sunday, throwing for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Brissett isn't the same kind of quarterback, but he has plenty of NFL experience and should have enough weapons around him to make an impact in his first game with Baltimore. I expect at least two of his passes to find the end zone Monday night. Zay Flowers could be in line for a productive performance, which would be welcome news for fantasy managers who have been waiting for the Ravens' offense to get back on track. Bold Prediction No. 2: Keaton Mitchell scores a touchdown against his former team This is probably the boldest prediction of the three. Mitchell will face his former team for the first time since joining the Chargers, and I think he'll find a way to make his return memorable. Mitchell has one touchdown this season, and it came through the air. He's recorded 46 carries for 178 yards, averaging 3.9 yards per attempt, while adding 18 receptions for 103 yards. The Chargers have continued to rotate their running backs, making it difficult to predict which player will receive the most opportunities. However, Mitchell has shown that he can contribute as both a runner and receiver. In primetime, I expect him to get a chance near the goal line and take advantage of it. Scoring against the team that gave him his NFL opportunity would make for a pretty good Monday night story. Bold Prediction No. 1: The Chargers win their first game of the 2026 season The Chargers have a chance to win? Yes, they do. Without Lamar Jackson under center, Baltimore is a much more vulnerable opponent. The Ravens are 4-5, dealing with injuries and trying to get their season back on track. Meanwhile, the Chargers are desperate to avoid falling to 0-9. There's also an interesting storyline on the sideline. Jesse Minter , who previously served as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, will face his former boss, Jim Harbaugh, for the first time as opposing head coaches. Harbaugh's first season in Los Angeles has been a disaster, but this is an opportunity to give his team something positive. Justin Herbert needs to play much better than he did against Houston, and I expect him to respond with a more competitive performance. Baltimore still has plenty of defensive talent. Marlon Humphrey and Roquan Smith could make things difficult for Herbert, while Kyle Hamilton would be another major factor if he's healthy enough to play. This could be an ugly game, with both offenses struggling to find consistency. However, I think the Chargers finally get over the hump and leave Baltimore with a victory. Score Prediction: Chargers win 20-17, with Cameron Dicker making four field goals. Los Angeles can't go 0-17, can it? This is one of its best remaining opportunities to avoid that nightmare, and I'm picking the Chargers to take advantage. away.headline: Move Over Substation, Chargers Have a New King of Injuries in LA with Week 10 Report
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-8, they just had a final hour trade before the trade deadline fall through and they are still searching for any sort of identity on offense. Los Angeles has been dealing with injuries all season long, by Week Six they already had over half of their original 53-man roster on the injury report or injured reserve. The Chargers injury luck is not improving much. For all the jokes and talk about the electrical substation near the San Francisco 49ers practice facility, Los Angeles may have something worse. The Chargers' practice facility, the Bolt, is located near Los Angeles International Airport, perhaps it's the air quality, or something in the the Los Angeles water or perhaps SoFi Stadium itself, something is up in LA. The Rams, who now have placed another wide receiver on injured reserve, may agree SoFi stadium, the Chargers and Rams' shared stadium, has a role in this. Both Los Angeles teams are in the top 10 of most injured this season in nearly every metric. The Chargers emerge from the NFL trade deadline with the exact same roster and will now head to Baltimore to take on the Jacoby Brissett-led Ravens on Monday Night Football. The Chargers will have a chance to steal their first win of the season as the Ravens search for their identity with a brand new quarterback at the helm but will their long list of injuries get in the way? It feels like groundhog day for the Chargers and their MASH unit of players following their loss to the Houston Texans. The Chargers have a significant portion of their cornerback room on the injury report. Tarheeb Still and Donte Jackson are the only cornerbacks not on the injury report to start the week of practice. The Chargers offensive line continues to be cursed. Guards Kayode Awosika, Alex Harkey and Branson Taylor are all on the injury report and Taylor was unable to practice at all after getting his first snaps of the season against Houston. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris are both on the report with McConkey missing the first practice of the week following suffering back spasms during pregame warmups prior to the week nine matchup against the Texans. The Chargers have had a revolving door at most positions on offense this season, which certainly has not helped their performance. As the Chargers, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and quarterback Justin Herbert continue to try to dial in the offense, their efforts are clearly made more of a challenge with the amount of injuries facing the unit. away.headline: Chargers Injury Report: 9 players sit out 1st practice of Week 10
away.blurb: Chargers Injury Report: 9 players sit out 1st practice of Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Chargers Injury Report: 9 players sit out 1st practice of Week 10 The Chargers began their prep for the Ravens with a whopping 18 players listed on their Thursday injury report. Of those players, over half of them sat out with a DNP tag. That group of nine included wide receiver Ladd McConkey (back), offensive guard/tackle Branson Taylor (ankle), defensive tackle Justin Eboigbe (ankle), and cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle). Every other player was given a limited designation. That group includes tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman, both of whom are likely to be activated this week off of IR. Offensive guard/tackle Trey Pipkins also had his practice window activated this week, although he did miss Thursday's practice altogether for personal reasons. Following the botched trade to the Broncos, linebacker Daiyan Henley was a DNP Thursday for personal reasons. Jim Harbaugh told reporters prior to practice that Henley got back to LA from Denver late Wednesday night and his attendance on Thursday was always going to be TBD. McConkey's injury continuing to keep him out of practice is worrisome. After being completely off the final injury report before the Texans game, he never made it onto the field as sudden back spasms kept him from playing. Now, four days later, those back spasms are still enough of a problem to keep him from practicing. This is most certainly something to monitor this week. home.blurb: "Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal," Minter said. "He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return." Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss between six and 10 weeks as he recovers from a broken and dislocated thumb, head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Friday. Jackson's health has been a primary storyline surrounding the Ravens throughout the 2026 campaign. First, he missed three games because of a high ankle sprain. While he returned for Baltimore's Week 8 game against the Buffalo Bills, he exited after his first snap with the thumb injury that required surgery. To make matters worse, Baltimore lost backup Tyler Huntley to a turf toe injury and had to turn to Joe Fagnano for the rest of the loss to the Bills and the entirety of the following loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Ravens scrambled and traded for Jacoby Brissett in an effort to weather the storm. Baltimore is looking to snap a four-game losing streak Monday night against the winless Los Angeles Chargers.

home.blurb: The Ravens ' head coach released a statement on Friday, Nov. 13 that gave an updated timeline for quarterback Lamar Jackson 's return from injury . The timeline that Minter provided suggests Jackson still has a chance to return by the end of the regular season. "Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take 6-10 weeks to heal," Minter's statement read. "He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return." Should Baltimore make the playoffs, it could see Jackson return in time to aid in a postseason push, per Minter's statement. The Ravens are currently 4-5 and in last place in the AFC North, but they're one game behind the 5-4 Patriots, who currently hold the conference's No. 7 seed. Here's everything to know about Jackson's injury and possible return this year: "Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8," the Ravens' head coach said in his statement. "Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return. The thumb injury is Jackson's second this season that will force him to miss time. The two-time MVP missed three games earlier this year with an ankle injury. His thumb injury occurred on the first play of his Week 8 return from the ailing ankle. Baltimore placed Jackson on injured reserve on Nov. 5. The Ravens' Week 9 game against the Jaguars was the first game Jackson missed due to his thumb injury. There is a chance he returns during the regular season, according to the recovery timeline Minter provided, but a postseason or 2027 return are more likely outcomes. home.headline: Ravens get devastating update on Lamar Jackson’s status
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens offered a clearer picture of Lamar Jackson’s recovery Friday but stopped short of setting a return date for their franchise quarterback. “Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.” Jackson injured his throwing hand on Baltimore’s first offensive play against Buffalo on November 1. His right hand struck Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau as he attempted a throw, immediately ending his return to the lineup. He had already missed three games with an ankle injury. Related Articles Kirk Cousins’ Vikings Return Comes With an Emotional Twist In a statement released by the team, head coach Jesse Minter said injuries like Jackson’s broken and dislocated thumb typically require six to 10 weeks to heal when surgery is necessary. The update leaves Baltimore preparing for an extended stretch without the two-time NFL MVP as it tries to reverse a four-game losing streak. “Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8,” Minter said. Minter described a typical healing window rather than announcing Jackson would miss another six to 10 weeks beginning Friday. The statement did not specify a target game or establish when that recovery window began. The Ravens’ quarterback problems worsened that afternoon when Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the second quarter. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finished the Buffalo game and started the following Thursday against Jacksonville. Baltimore lost those games 36-10 and 33-10, respectively, falling to 4-5. Following the loss, the Ravens made a trade to acquire Jacoby Brissett from Arizona on November 6. The veteran is preparing to make his first Baltimore start Monday night against the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) while learning a new offense on an accelerated schedule. “It’s definitely a crash course. No question,” Brissett said Thursday. Baltimore has scored no more than 13 points in any game during its four-game skid. Brissett’s immediate assignment is to restore enough offensive consistency to stop that slide. Jackson has not abandoned the possibility of returning this season. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport previously reported that he told teammates he intended to come back, although his recovery and Baltimore’s ability to remain competitive will shape that possibility. The Ravens need to keep their season alive while Jackson recovers. That responsibility now falls to Brissett, whose first start Monday offers Baltimore a chance to end its four-game skid and give its injured quarterback something to come back to.
